chapters.title: Chapter 101: Activating The Compass
paragraphs: Kent lay back, a smile playing on his lips as he replayed the video in his mind.

The look on his face throughout the process was etched into his memory as he recalled how domineering he had been—the intense energy he felt, the arrogance, the power, and the finesse with which he carried himself.
It all came rushing back to him, and for a moment, he felt invincible. However, he knew it was just the euphoria.

There was no way in hell he could compare his current self to the persona he saw in the video. He might be stronger than the average human at the moment, but he was nothing compared to the domineering version of himself in that vision.
Strangely, the aura he exuded in the video was that of a Root Grandmaster, yet it was several times thicker than the aura of a peak Root Sage.
And if that wasn’t shocking enough, he had emanated Sword Will—the stage beyond sword intent, achieved only after mastering all nine levels of it.
The scene was overwhelming, and Kent craved that power. He wanted to feel it in his bones.
[The master should stop daydreaming and focus on what he can handle now.] The tower, however, seemed displeased with Kent’s behaviour.
"Fine. But once I claim that power, I’ll make sure to cause some chaos of my own," Kent said with a smirk, deciding to put the matter aside for now.
It was time to start preparing for his trip to the Realm of Hatred and Resentment—the god realm where Vexthra resided.
After receiving the three wishes from the enchantress, Kent’s first wish was for a way to travel the universe without significant restrictions.
Of course, he wasn’t a fool. He understood that venturing into unknown places could be perilous, so his wish was carefully tailored toward accessing the one place he currently desired—the god realm.
Specifically, the Realm of Hatred and Resentment.
Kent retrieved the [Starbound Compass] and appraised it once more.
Starbound Compass
-- A mystical compass with a needle made of stardust, pointing unerringly toward the desired destination when activated. The compass projects a portal for travel.
Activation Requirements:
- Spirit Stones: 10,000,000,000 (Max)
- Soul Essence: 100,000 (Max)
Cooldown Time:
- Once requirements are met, the orb needs 96 hours to activate.
- Once used, the orb goes into a 60-day cooldown.
Limitations:
- You will be forcefully returned after 72 hours.
- The portal can be closed using the portal, but if the user doesn’t return within 72 hours, they will be forcefully pulled back.
- The user can return any item provided they can be stored in their soul. Space rings are not allowed.
[Note: Before using any of the three items, you must know where you want to go.]
The price was pretty high, but it wasn’t a problem for him. However, the main issue was knowledge—he must know where he wants to go before he opens the portal.
For him, he had been there before, but only when he died.
He wasn’t sure if that would count. Of course, he’d find out once the compass finished charging.
For now, all he knew was that ten billion spirit stones were the maximum one needed to pay to activate the compass.
This meant that even if he knew a location at the far end of the universe, he would only be required to pay ten billion spirit stones.

This also meant that if he travelled a shorter distance, the chances of paying less were quite high. Essentially, after the tower performed a few diagnostics, it determined that soul essence and spirit stones served merely as fuel.
He wouldn’t need to pay again if the fuel were still burning within it.
"Tower, feed ten billion spirit stones to the compass," Kent instructed. The spirit stones were securely absorbed into the compass in the next second.
He then retrieved the next item, the soul bead. The moment it appeared, a dense soul essence flooded the space.

From the video, he had seen how the bead was made, yet nothing seemed to surface in his mind, no matter how hard he tried to recall what went into its creation. In the end, he could only continue with what he had.
[Extreme Soul Bead (Forbidden Pill)]
[Grade: Tier 7]
-- This bead has been condensed from a human’s soul and life force. It has also been amplified using forbidden dark magic, making it 3000 times more potent.
-- But although the bead is forbidden, it contains the purest form of soul energy.
-- Absorbing this bead will enhance one’s soul in many ways. It also nurtures the soul and makes it very rich in concentration.
-- It is said that if a soul cultivator absorbs a soul bead, their chances of forming a soul body are very high. It also improves the spirit root to a certain degree.
"How I wish I could create this myself," Kent muttered, staring intently at the bead in his hand. If he could absorb all the soul essence within it, he could elevate his soul cultivation to Tier 7.
His current level was only Tier 2, comparable to a Root Blossom Expert. However, he wasn’t about to waste time.
"Tower, you know what to do," Kent said.

The tower extracted 100,000 essences from the bead to fuel the compass. Once everything was completed, Kent activated the compass. He channelled his soul energy into it and dropped a single drop of blood onto it to make it his soul item.
It would take 92 hours—nearly four days—to fully activate.
During that time, the compass would register all the major places Kent had ever visited and the locations it could access. He could open a portal to any of these places with just a single tap.
With the activation underway, Kent decided to focus on something else while waiting for the 92 hours to reach.
He had already given the skills they had purchased to the ladies on their way home. While he would have loved to spend time with them during the wait, he knew they would be very busy.
Of course, he was well aware that the moment he entered the god realm, he and Vexthra would have a rather long three-day marathon. He was looking forward to that.
Once everything was set, Kent placed the bead down and began absorbing the essence to boost his soul cultivation while waiting for the compass to activate.
Right now, he was driven by the desire to grow stronger. Part of this stemmed from the scene he had seen in the video—he wanted that strength.
For someone destined to go against a god, Kent knew that, with or without memories of his past self, he would soon become a monster.
Fortunately, he had the tower, which held everything he needed to become who he was meant to be. Without even realizing it, Kent had already begun walking the path.
With Spiritual Qi and Soul Cultivation already underway, the next step would be tempering his body and embarking on Body Cultivation.
His path was set, and a new Chaos Lord would soon be born.

chapters.title: Chapter 102: Entering the god realm
paragraphs: [Master, the compass is now activated, and you can use it to enter the god realm anytime now]
3 days, 20 hours later, the tower informed Kent that the compass had activated. He snapped open his eyes and stored away the soul bead.
Instead of going straight for the compass to open the portal, he first looked at the messages that appeared during his soul cultivation.
[You have absorbed enough soul essence to level up]
[You have levelled up. Current Level: 3. +100 added to soul strength.]
========Soul Cultivation========
[Class Name: Soul Cultivator (Spirit Master)]
[Soul Essense: 7045]
[Level: Tier 3]
[Progress Meter: 7045/10,008]
"Looks like soul cultivation is much slower than spiritual qi cultivation," Kent muttered, staring at the data before him.

[Indeed. However, because of the ’Soul Absorb’ skill the master possesses, killing spirit beasts and other creatures will speed up the process significantly. The skill allows you to absorb nearly 99% of the soul essence from those you kill.

But since the master has the soul bead with immense essence, the master could invest in something called a ’Soul Absorption Talisman.’ It’s a Tier 6 talisman that can accelerate the absorption process.]
"I see. But where can I get one? I need to be able to activate the compass manually. With my current soul strength, it would take me days to feed it the 100,000 soul essence when it runs dry.
Relying too much on my precious soul bead isn’t ideal. I feel like there’s more to the bead, and I don’t want to waste it this early."
[The tower has some, but the master must first become a Grandmaster to awaken them. Until then, the master will have to focus on using the manual method.]
Kent sighed. He doesn’t want to waste the bead on just activating the compass.
A part of the description of the bead was:
-- It is said that if a soul cultivator absorbs a soul bead, their chances of forming a soul body are very high. It also improves the spirit root to a certain degree.
Soul body. He had inquired of the tower, and according to it, a soul body is an ethereal form derived from his soul, possessing numerous abilities he can wield in both battles and cultivation.

The tower explained that he could even use his soul body to enter the spirit realm, where, according to the scriptures on soul cultivation, his chances of encountering a fortuitous event that could elevate his soul to its peak are highly favourable.
Additionally, the tower revealed that if his soul body reaches a certain stage, even if he dies, he can reform his physical body from his soul body—provided it escapes before his death.
It offered countless uses, and because of that, Kent wasn’t content to use it as fuel for the compass.
If he managed to push his soul essence to [50,000], he would need only two days to power the compass. However, that would depend entirely on the strength of his resolve to cultivate his soul.
For now, he could only focus on what he could handle and what he could not.
He left his room to inform his two ladies that he would be away for the next three days.
"Kent, I know you don’t want us to know where you’re going, but please be careful, okay? We don’t want you getting hurt," Unity said, lying against his chest.
He came to tell them about his absence, fully expecting the two vixens to coax him into bed—but he never expected them to go three rounds each.
Ultimately, he allowed them to have their way and "violate" little Kent.
"I promise, where I’m going, no harm will come to me." Since the two ladies were connected to Vexthra, Kent wasn’t about to tell them he was heading to the god realm.
They would spoil the surprise.
Instead, he planned to shock them from the god realm. That would be far more entertaining. For one, Kent was eager to sense their reactions.
The harem connection allowed him to feel the emotions of his ladies. Right now, he could sense their determination to grow stronger and assist him outside the bedroom.
"Kent, when you come back, I want to talk to you about my mother," Lilian said shyly.
"Okay. I hope she’s doing alright. It’s been a while since I last saw her," Kent replied.
Though he was practically living with them, he hadn’t truly paid much attention to their lives. In fact, it had been quite a while since he’d seen her.
"Mom is fine. Just go and come back. We’ll talk then," Lilian responded.
A while later, he freshened up and went to talk to his master.

His master was training when Kent arrived, while Li Hua was busy baking banana cakes. She had used some of the money she got from Saintess Selene during their shopping spree to buy the necessary equipment and ingredients.
"Can I have one?" Kent asked, making Li Hua turn around in surprise.
"Big Brother! Look, I baked some banana cakes," Li Hua exclaimed, jumping into Kent’s arms. She was overjoyed to see him.
"I see you’ve returned to your old profession. Are you planning to go back to selling banana cakes?" Kent teased with a grin.
"No, I just want to sell cakes to Big Brother," Li Hua replied, flashing a cute little smile.
"Oh, really? How much for one?" Kent asked, amused, knowing full well the little human was scheming to lighten his wallet.

"Because it’s Big Brother, I’ll only charge 100 spirit stones for one... No, wait—1,000 spirit stones for one cake! What do you think? Would you like to buy my delicious cakes?" Li Hua asked, her expression suddenly serious, resembling a determined businesswoman.
"I’ll take them all," Kent said without hesitation. He retrieved 30,000 spirit stones and handed them over before picking up the 30 banana cakes from the tray.
"Thanks for doing business with you, big brother," Li Hua said, immediately returning to her baking after selling her first batch.
Kent just smiled and shook his head.

"Li Hua, I’ll be going somewhere for the next three days. You must stay with your mother and never step outside this place. When I get back, I’ll take you sightseeing," Kent said. Li Hua simply nodded and continued baking.
Kent walked toward his master, who had paused her training to speak with him. Of course, Kent wasn’t about to miss the chance to tease her.
He stepped closer and wrapped his arm around her waist.
"I’ll be gone for three days, Master. Don’t miss me too much. Also, I promise I’ll be safe," Kent said as he pulled her closer, kissing her cheek before letting go.
With laughter in the air, he teleported away. Saintess Selene’s hand touched her cheek, which had suddenly turned red.
’This bastard, how can he be so shameless?’ she blushed.
The past few days had been a battle with her heart from what Kent said before they parted. And now, just when she was regaining her resolve, this bastard had planted yet another seed in her heart.
She stopped training and went to sit beside Li Hua. She will need a few hours to get her mind off things.

chapters.title: Chapter 103: The Goddess is Happy (1) [18+]
paragraphs: Somewhere in the Realm of Hatred and Resentment, Vexthra, who had committed to living the life of a mortal to keep her sanity in check, woke up with a drowsy look.

She entered the bathroom and brushed her teeth. Afterward, she decided to stretch, loosening her mortal muscles. In fact, she had hidden her divinity and suppressed her cultivation base to that of a mortal.
So, everything she did was what a mortal would do. That was the reality for a goddess who had experienced an entire year of pleasure with her man.
After stretching, she made tea and sat down to read a few Chapters of a popular web novel that had been trending for the past two years.
"Don’t be a crybaby, Sunny; Neph is the best person to become your master. I wouldn’t mind making my man my master. After all, just like you love Neph, I do too," Vexthra commented aloud.
She was engrossed in a Chapter about a shadow human who was complaining because the lady he loved had used his True Name to enslave him in order to save his life.
Soon, she became completely absorbed in the novel, and before she realized it, it was almost five in the evening. Setting the book aside, she got up to prepare dinner.
However, just as she stepped off the bed, a purple portal opened before her.
In an instant, a sword appeared in her hand, ready for whatever uninvited presence might emerge.
The tension dissipated and the sword also vanished as a confident, handsome, purple-haired young man stepped through the portal.
"Hello there. Is this the Realm of Hatred and Resentment? Smells familiar, but I’m not entirely sure," Kent said with a smile, his gaze meeting Vexthra’s.
Her eyes turned a rosy hue as she stared at Kent’s strikingly handsome face.
"Kent, is it really you?" Vexthra asked, momentarily forgetting she could use her divinity to appraise and confirm if this was indeed her man, Kent.

Kent smiled and stepped closer to her. He pulled her by the waist and planted a kiss on her lips. This gesture alone melted Vexthra’s heart, proving to her that her man had indeed found his way back to her.
"Does this answer your question?" Kent asked as he pulled back.
"Kent, it really is you!" Vexthra exclaimed, wrapping her arms around his neck and burying her face in his chest as tears ran down her cheeks.
’My aura is that damn contagious. Even the embodiment of hatred and resentment couldn’t resist,’ Kent bragged inwardly as he rubbed her back.
[The master has indeed changed her,] the tower was quick to comment.
Vexthra stayed buried in Kent’s chest for a few more moments before finally pulling back.
"How... how are you here?" she asked, her voice trembling.
"Never doubt me, Vexthra. I promised you I would find my way to you, and here I am," Kent replied, lifting her by the waist and wrapping her legs around him.
"Now, this is what’s going to happen. For the next three days, we are going to have so much sex that, when I’m gone, the feeling will stick with you for months."
Kent walked toward the bed and effortlessly tossed Vexthra onto it. He then closed the portal with a wave of his hand and leaped onto the overly large bed.

The kiss resumed, but this time, it was far more intense. Vexthra clung to Kent as though afraid this moment might slip away, her arms wrapped tightly around him. She savored the sensation, unsure if it was real or just another vivid dream.
She had been plagued by dreams lately, and now she wanted to confirm this was no illusion he had conjured.
After a few moments, Vexthra seemed to have her answer. A spark of certainty flared within her, and she chose to lose herself in the moment.
She shifted, turning Kent onto his back, and gazed into his eyes before diving back into the kiss.
This time, the goddess abandoned all restraint, ensuring Kent felt her hunger as their tongues intertwined in a fierce battle for dominance.
"You missed me that much, huh?" Kent teased, licking his lips as he met Vexthra’s crimson gaze—once filled with hatred and resentment, now brimming with warmth and love.
"Shut up and fuck me," Vexthra commanded, shoving him back down and ripping his shirt apart in one swift motion.
"Hey, that was very expensive, okay?" Kent complained, glancing at the now shredded fabric.
"I’ll compensate you," Vexthra replied with a sly smile as she loosened his trousers. In moments, those, too, were torn away, leaving Kent naked with his semi-ready manhood on full display.
Vexthra wasted no time. She wrapped her lips around his dick, her tongue skillfully gliding along his length. Her movements were precise yet passionate, sending Kent spiraling into bliss.
The sensation was otherworldly, perhaps due to Vexthra’s divine nature. Everything about her seemed to radiate an irresistible allure, even the way she tasted.
Her tongue danced around Kent’s length, making him smile while he moaned and groaned slightly.
"Damn goddess"
Kent suddenly shouted as his dick entered Vexthra’s throat, making her gag. She was literally swallowing his dick like there was no tomorrow.

’Is that thing perhaps against divinity?’ Kent wondered.
[I don’t think so, Master.
However, I believe this is an opportunity for us to get some answers about the compass.
The goddess seems to know more about it.
Do well to learn something, Master.]
The tower summarized the situation quickly, urging Kent to make the most of this chance.
The Compass is a mystery he doesn’t have the means to uncover just yet.
It took Vexthra 20 minutes to finally regain her strength and composure.
"Sorry about that.
I was just too shocked seeing that thing," Vexthra said with a forced smile.
"Vex, do you know what that thing is?
If you know anything, please tell me," Kent urged.
As the tower had pointed out, he knew this was his chance to uncover more about the compass and its true potential.
Vexthra didn’t answer right away.
She looked at Kent, studying his expression and trying to gauge his readiness and willingness to learn about the Starbound Compass.
Indeed, she was doing just that.
But she was hesitant, uncertain whether she should say anything at all.
Just as she was deciding, a voice echoed in her mind.
’Tell him.’
That was all it said, but it was enough to make her change her mind.
"Listen to me and listen well, Kent.
That compass is something nobody—not even Unity and Lilian—should know about.
In fact, if there is a way, I would like to forget about this after today," Vexthra said grimly.
’I will do just that.
You have nothing to worry about.
I won’t allow any harm to come to you,’ the voice spoke again.
Vexthra seemed to have calmed down yet again.
"That compass is one of the seven most dangerous things in the universe.
In fact, if they were ranking the seven, this compass would be at the third spot.
I know you don’t know much about it, and that is for the best.
But to tell you what danger you are in, I will first tell you a story.
Please remember every single thing."
’Tower, record everything.’
[Way ahead of you, master.]
"Go on, dear," Kent said.
Vexthra sighed.
"Long ago, a peculiar race of beings known as the Gxxyla referred to as travellers because they specialise in travelling to distant worlds and realms.
They once time chanced upon something that changed their lives since that day.
Before that, you should know the origin of this compass.
When this universe came into existence, it was said that a very dangerous battle occurred—a battle meant to determine whether this universe would live or die.
In the end, we won, and it survived.
However, it came at a cost.
It was said that during that battle, which took place in the primordial era, 13 beings of great and unfathomable power fought for the survival of this universe.
It was a chaotic battle, but we emerged victorious.
Yet, the price was steep.
When the battle reached its climax, one of the 13 sacrificed his life to launch a final attack, ending the chaotic battle.
In doing so, his soul shattered into seven pieces.
These seven fragments became what we now know as the seven Primordial Chaos Treasures.
But before anyone could claim them, the remaining 12 of his comrades cast a powerful spell to send the seven items to the farthest corners of the universe, hidden from both time and reach.
Somehow, one of these items was found by the Gxxyla—a race of travellers who, back then, would journey vast distances across the cosmos.
After acquiring this compass, their nature transformed.
They became a race that could traverse any distance, enter any realm, and remain unstoppable.
Legend has it that they could even infiltrate the Supreme and Celestial realms without being challenged by any force or law.
However, their arrogance led to their downfall.
They infiltrated a realm that belonged to creatures of the unknown.
It is said that their reckless actions unknowingly created a rift, connecting this universe to a race whose sole purpose is the destruction of universes—the Helian Race.
Because of this connection, our universe is once again in grave danger.
The gateway they opened is said to bring calamity upon us all one day.
However, a prophecy declares that to avert this catastrophe, the seven Primordial Chaos Treasures must be found and assembled.
And thus, for millions of years, people, including gods, have been searching for these seven treasures.
Many races went extinct because of these items," Vexthra sighs again.
"This is dangerous because, right now, the Helian Race, which managed to infiltrate this universe before the gateway was sealed, is also searching for it.
Do you know what this means?
If the beings of this universe and the Helian Race discover that you possess this compass, one of the seven Primordial Treasures, they will do everything they can to take it from you.
After all, many races in this universe are in cohorts with the Helian Race.
This is dangerous, Kent."

chapters.title: Chapter 106: The Enchantress Connection
paragraphs: Kent didn’t immediately ask anything. His mind cycled through a whirlwind of pondering as if trying to grasp something just out of reach, yet he lacked any understanding of the origin story.
But that didn’t mean he had nothing to say.
"You said this item is one of the Seven Primordial Chaos Treasures. Do you know the names of the others?" Kent asked.
Perhaps knowing them would bring him some clarity. While he didn’t know much, his subconscious was working to uncover something.
"I only know of one other," Vexthra replied. "Aside from the compass, only one other item has been discovered. As for the rest, their names were once known but have faded from memory over time.
"Of course, you might wonder how I know the danger ranking level of the compass if I don’t know the names of the other five.
"The answer is simple: I am a goddess.

"The other of the Seven Primordial Chaos Treasures is the Hidden Celestial Library Key. It was discovered many ages ago, but it is currently inaccessible to anyone except an Enchantress who is forever bound to her temple," Vexthra explained.
"I see. So she is connected, huh?" Kent muttered, shaking his head.
It all started to make sense. The Enchantress was the one in possession of one of the Seven Primordial Chaos Treasures. But that was a different one.
If she once possessed one of the items, did that mean she knew the location of the others? After all, she had given Kent the compass—who’s to say she couldn’t do the same for the other treasures?
Suddenly, a desire sparked within Kent—a wish to find the remaining Seven Primordial Chaos Treasures. But he knew wishes didn’t work like that. Greed would only make him lose his remaining wishes.

Still, that was just speculation. Kent had another thought, one that intrigued him even more. Now that he possessed the compass, could he sense the other items, as he assumed the Enchantress might have?
"Kent, tell me the Enchantress has nothing to do with this compass. Please, tell me," Vexthra, who had overheard his muttering, asked with a frown.
Kent just gave her a guilty smile. The enchantress was indeed connected to the compass. After all, it was through her that he managed to acquire it.
"Unbelievable," Vexthra didn’t know what to say.
"Just how did you come into contact with her? You are in a realm far from her, so how did you manage to get her attention?" Vexthra asked.

She had sent Kent to a medium world so he wouldn’t be in danger. Yet, in just a few months, he had not only acquired one of the Seven Primordial Chaos Treasures but also gained the attention of the last Ancient Enchantress.
"You know. I’m awesome to the point that a whole enchantress found me cute and gave me three wishes. One thing led to another, and here I am," Kent said with a small smile.
Vexthra just shook her head and then froze.
"Please tell me you didn’t inherit the Enchantress’s Favor, her quest," she asked again.

"Is that bad? I indeed inherited it, but it came with great rewards." Kent wasn’t particularly concerned about Vexthra’s panic. She used to hate and resent, so maybe she was now learning other emotions.
"What other rewards?" Vexthra asked.
"Well, she gave me access to the Quest Pool. Now I can obtain any quest I want, depending on the realm I am in, my strength, professions, and awesomeness."
"Oh my god!" Vexthra shouted, not having the strength to comprehend what was happening.
"You are a goddess, why are you shouting ’oh my god’? Don’t tell me you’re cheating on me with another god," Kent playfully narrowed his eyes.
He could tell the goddess was going through a lot, so he gave her some time to breathe.
"First, she gave you the Starbound Compass using the only loophole, which is Wishes, and then she also gave you access to the quest pool. Do you know what this means, Kent?" Vexthra asked.

"I will tell you. This means that from now on, you will become the sole owner of the quest pool. In fact, throughout the history of the universe, only 13 others had access to this quest pool, and only one person at a time.

You can now access all the rewards the universe can offer through quests. You also have access to all the amazing adventures the universe has in store for its children. This means you have become the one and only child of the universe.
This means you have, without even knowing it, become the sole defender of the Universe. Kent, your life has, in a way, become more amazing yet also dangerous within just a few months.
This is bad. Very bad." Vexthra wiped an invisible sweat off her forehead.
"At this rate, you will become the centre of danger now that you have the pool. The universe will want you to become the defender if anything goes wrong.
Though it will give you great rewards, it will also put you in danger every now and then."
"I don’t mind danger. If I’m going to kill a god, the least I can do is handle the dangers along the journey.
And hey, don’t worry about me. I won’t be alone. Your sisters will be with me, and I also have the tower with me. My life won’t be in any danger," Kent said with a small smile.
Vexthra sighed and made a mental note to hasten the training of the two ladies she now called sisters. While Kent might not know it yet, his life was indeed in grave danger.
But for now, Vexthra didn’t want to say much, knowing it would only affect him more than do him any good.
’Please don’t wipe these memories from me,’ Vexthra thought, realizing her initial fear of not knowing about the Compass was now something she needed to remember to help Kent.
’Don’t worry, you will remember, but you should be prepared to do anything when he is in danger,’ the voice said to her.
’I will. I will do anything, including giving up my divinity if it means ensuring his safety,’ Vexthra vowed in her heart.
’Very well. I will listen to you, my daughter,’ the Voice spoke.
’Thank you, Mother,’ Vexthra sighed.
"Is there anything else you want to tell me? I only know the Compass’s origin, but not how to use it. I also know that the Enchantress’s heart is the second of the Seven Primordial Chaos items.

I also know that the enchantress is very dangerous; however, she is also very trustworthy. For now, don’t use your other two wishes lightly. You have to think about what you want and weigh the pros and cons before taking any action.

Also, ensure nobody besides you knows about the Compass and the Quest Pool. But know this: when you ask for a quest, you can reject it, but when the Universe gives a quest, no matter how unreasonable or dangerous, never reject it.
That’s all I know. Now, before you leave, is there something I should know?" Vexthra didn’t want to miss anything.

chapters.title: Chapter 107: Gossip with A Goddess (1)
paragraphs: "I have a lot of things to share with you. It’s just that I don’t know where to start," Kent said, pondering where to begin.
Vexthra was the one who pulled out his soul and brought him to her realm, where she gave him another chance at life. This means he exists now because of her.

And since he can’t actively talk to her like Lilian and Unity could, it was only natural for her to ask and Kent to tell. After all, he plans to squeeze her for some things he intends to take back to the mortal realm.
"Let me start with my cultivation and progress so far in Alchemy," Kent finally decided.
"I have finally managed to become a Master stage Alchemist with a Purity Level of 100%," Kent said with a cute smile. Vexthra just smiled.
Unity and Lilian had already told her all about Kent’s amazing pills. Although it sounded amazing that he had achieved a hundred per cent purity, it wasn’t something new to her.
However, as a pill master, it was indeed impressive to have 100% purity when he had only started a few weeks ago. Those practising for years couldn’t boast of such an achievement.
"Those two vixens will pay for spoiling my surprise," Kent smiled.
"I assume you’ve already informed them I am here with you," Kent chose to ask, knowing Vexthra may have already ruined the plan he had in mind.
And he was right. She had indeed informed them that Kent was with her and that she would give him some trinkets to bring to them when he returned.
"Annoying bunch," Kent muttered before choosing to focus on the next thing.
"I have also awakened a sword body. Cool, right?" Kent said, looking rather smug.
His master had already told him he shouldn’t have been able to awaken a sword body just yet. He should have at least reached the Grandmaster sword stage first before that would have been possible.
Yet the fact that he had somehow awakened it said a lot about how talented he was.
"Before I comment on anything, take this space ring and only open it when you go back." Kent received the space ring and placed it in the tower storage.
"Now, as for whether you’ve awakened a sword body, it is cool, but there’s no need to look so smug. Your current sword body is not that impressive," Vexthra said with a teasing smile.
Kent immediately grabbed her ass and gave it a gentle squeeze, applying the [Divine Pervert Touch] with the intent of making her feel extreme horniness.
And it worked.
Her little sister released a few tears, soaking the bed.
"I am sorry, please stop," Vexthra laughed through the extreme lust coursing through her body. Kent stopped, looking smug yet again.
"What was that?" Vexthra asked. The feeling she experienced just now was rather nice, yet she felt things could go bad for her if Kent chose to.
"I won’t tell you," Kent teased.

"Fine. I will find out soon enough. As for your sword body, know that after fledging, which you currently are at, there are other stages. Until you reach the 4th stage, the current you can’t be called a prodigy," Vexthra said, her words making Kent smile.
At the moment, he wasn’t about to claim he was a prodigy. No, he had only started cultivating a few months ago. He may be awesome, but he was still inexperienced.
However, that didn’t mean he was weak, either. He already had Sword Intent, Sword Qi, and Sword Body. As a swordsman, he needed these three essentials to walk the path.
But there were stages to it, and he couldn’t be proud of his current stage. Though, at his level, he looks cool for having all three.
"You need to progress from Fledging, Copper, Bronze, Silver, and Gold before you can step into the path of a real sword body.

If you want the most amazing body possible, focus more on tempering your body. Trust me, when you achieve gold bodies for both sword body and body cultivation, your path forward will be smooth sailing."
"Thank you for your kind teaching, my goddess. I will focus more on that," Kent said sarcastically.
"Next," Vexthra said, extending her hand toward little Kent, who was already up and strong.

"I now have a master. She’s very beautiful and, well, very strong. I plan on making her your third sister," Kent said, imagining the look that would appear on Saintess Selene’s face when he drilled her tiny hole with his divine rod.

"I know, and I have to say, your charm is rather weak. I expected to have dozens of sisters by now, but it seems you’re not that awesome," Vexthra giggled, holding onto Kent’s dick to prevent him from using the strange power on her again.
Kent, of course, wasn’t stupid. With his dick held hostage, he only smiled and answered like a good boy.
"Just so you know, I’m not a dog that chases any meat. And hey, it’s been only two months. Give me some credit for having two women already," Kent said, knowing he was indeed wasting his potential.
With his harem abilities, he wouldn’t even have to worry about cultivating if he had a dozen women by now.
Just having them cultivated manually would bless him with loads of spiritual qi. Plus, sleeping with them would provide endless benefits. He could have become a Saint by now.

"I know you don’t want to add just anyone to the harem, Kent, but you have dual cultivation. It’s not like you’re stealing from them. Those you sleep with will also benefit. In fact, they will benefit more than you.
So, holding back and not having fun is your own doing. Just so you know, until you become immortal, none of us will restrict you from sleeping with any woman you find to your liking.
Also, you can add any woman to the harem. As long as I remain a goddess, I will turn all of them into powerful cultivators within a year.

The events in your life now are too much to handle alone. You need a powerful army, and although it’s weird to say, having an army of women who love you is better than having an army of soldiers you can’t fully trust.

So stop restricting yourself and use this chance to have fun. You can start with your master, who, from what I’ve heard so far, is awesome and powerful. She’ll be a great addition," Vexthra said with a hint of unease.
Right now, she was worried about Kent—not because of the fact that he would be helping her kill a god, but because she loved him and didn’t want any harm to come to him.
"It feels weird getting advice to chase women from my own wife," Kent muttered with a defeated smile.
He had been using Vexthra as a standard to pick his women, but now, hearing it from his first wife, he figured he was just being ignorant.
Also, he is using Earth’s beliefs to do his things, forgetting he is now in a new world where morality is put in question.

"Yeah, well, get used to it. You have to use what I created to make women happy. Do you know how many bored women out there are waiting for your dick to cheer them up?" Vexthra asked with a teasing expression.

Uncle Drew, despite being on the verge of death, used the last of his strength to clench Kent’s hand, signalling that he could still hear him.
"Uncle Drew, don’t die on me! I still need you to take me to town and all the places I want to go. Please, don’t die," Kent pleaded, subconsciously praying to the gods for a miracle.
’Tower, do something,’ Kent desperately reached out to his only trusted assistant.
[I’m sorry, Master. With me still not fully awakened, I can’t do anything to save him,] the Tower responded, its words only adding to Kent’s despair.
’Think of something else! If he dies, I will—’

[The Master can use one of his wishes, but I can’t guarantee it will bring the dead back to life. From what I can sense, he is half-dead, and in the next thirty seconds, if nothing changes, he will be gone for good.
So, while the wish may not guarantee success, it’s your best shot,] the Tower advised.
’Thanks, Tower.’
Kent immediately decided to wish Uncle Drew back to good health. However, just as he was about to speak his wish, a voice echoed in his head.
’A rider is neither dead nor alive; a rider is a rider because they chose to ride at night. The Riders of the Night need to rise and ride again. Call forth the captain of the Riders of the Night.’
Hearing those words, something clicked in Kent’s mind, prompting him to shift from his current though and take on something else. He reached into his tower storage and retrieved an item.
It was the True Name Token he intended to use on Unity.
He planned to use the [True Name Token] to bestow a true name upon Uncle Drew. The reason was that the voice wanted that, and he wouldn’t hesitate.
’Tower, how do I use it?’ Kent asked.
[Drop your blood and his blood on it.] The tower seemed to gain some clarity as it replied.
Under the watchful eyes of the four ladies in the room, Kent dropped his blood on the token and then proceeded to drop Uncle Drew’s blood on it.
[A suitable true name has been rewarded. You can bestow it by chanting these incantations.]
Kent felt the information flood into his mind. Suddenly, he tapped Uncle Drew’s chest and began reciting the words.

"In the shadow of death and under the gaze of the eternal moon, I call forth the name that binds fate and defies the void. Let your soul be rekindled, and your strength become unyielding. Rise anew as the bearer of the mantle, Kael Duskbane’s legacy, and take upon yourself the True Name—Umbra Severis!"
"Rise, Umbra Severis, Captain of the Night Riders."
The moment Kent spoke those words, a surge of shadowy energy erupted from Uncle Drew’s body, instantly closing the wound on his chest.
But it didn’t stop there.
The shadowy energy continued pouring out, enveloping Uncle Drew in a cocoon of darkness. The room became thick with its oppressive aura as the energy surged for ten minutes before finally subsiding.
Then, something unexpected happened. The horse that had drawn Uncle Drew’s carriage mysteriously appeared in the room, standing vigil before the cocoon.

With a sudden, powerful burst, the cocoon shattered. Uncle Drew emerged, his complexion pale and shadowy. His eyes now glowed a vivid green, and his physique had transformed into that of a seasoned warrior.
He walked toward the horse, his movements deliberate and commanding, and climbed onto its back.
The moment he sat down, another wave of dark energy engulfed him and the horse. Their forms began to change.
The horse became spectral, its skeletal frame gleaming with an eerie brilliance, while Uncle Drew transformed into a figure of myth and legend.

His attire was jet black, adorned with intricate runic patterns that shimmered faintly in the dim light. A dark hood obscured half his face, and his armour appeared forged from bones, exuding an aura of unrelenting menace.
His eyes had shifted to a deep, glowing green, burning like twin embers beneath the shadow of his hood. On his back were two long swords, radiating potent dark energy that seemed almost alive.

Now fully transformed, the horse stood as a Shadowmare—an apex predator of battlefields, a spectral steed known only in legends. Its skeletal body glowed faintly, and its presence alone could strike fear into the hearts of the bravest.
Uncle Drew, now reborn as a Night Rider, turned to Kent. For a few tense moments, he simply stared, his piercing gaze assessing his summoner. Then, in a deep, resonant voice, he spoke.
"The night shall be ours again."
Kent smiled, his expression calm. As if guided by instinct, he responded.
"And they shall appear on the battlefields again. Their legend will rise once more, known as the harbingers of Hell, the creatures of myth—the Night Riders.
Oh, mighty Kael Duskbane, take your swords again and lead the Riders of the Night into the darkness. Let your legend be reborn."
Suddenly, a swirling portal materialized in the room. Without hesitation, Uncle Drew and his Shadowmare stepped into it and vanished.
The Captain of the Night Riders was born, and his mission was clear now.
He would seek out his fellow riders, awakening their slumbering legends and bringing them to their new master—Kent—who would bestow their true names and reignite their eternal saga once again.

chapters.title: Chapter 111: Curing His Master
paragraphs: The portal closed when Uncle Drew, now known as Kael Duskbane, the Captain of the Night Riders, passed through it with his Shadowmare steed.
Kent sighed.
He didn’t know how it all happened, but somehow, he knew exactly what to do and how to do it, which resulted in Uncle Drew becoming a Night Rider.
"I will see you soon, Uncle Drew," Kent said before turning to his women, Cynthia and Saintess Selene.
’Are you ladies alright?’ Kent used the telepathic connection between them to ask his women.
’Yes, but your master is not well. Attend to her first; we are not hurt or anything,’ Unity replied, making Kent thank his lucky stars.
While he wouldn’t have blamed his actions for choosing to spend time with his first wife, he certainly would have blamed himself for not being there if something had happened to them.
In fact, Lilian and Unity only decide to inform Vexthra when Kent’s master arrives hurt and Uncle Drew is dying. They would have waited for him to come back naturally if they had been alright.
"I will be taking my master away. Lilian, kindly look after your mother. Unity, come for Li Hua," Kent said, taking Saintess Selene into a princess carry.
Unity stepped beside him.
"Hold my waist," Kent said, and Unity followed. The next second, they vanished and appeared in Saintess Selene’s bedroom.
Li Hua, who was inside the room, immediately ran toward Saintess Selene, but Kent stopped her by telling her to go with Unity while her mother rested.
Li Hua obeyed and left with Unity. Kent doesn’t want her to get traumatized by seeing Saintess Selene, who she has chosen as her mother, hurt.
She was still recovering from her Grandma’s death.
Kent then placed Saintess Selene on the bed, who was still bleeding from the cut on her back.
’Tower, what are we dealing with?’ Kent asked.
[The attack was inflicted with a poison-infused weapon. The poison is Shadowbane Venom, known for slowing the body’s natural healing process.]
’Can it be cured?’ Kent asked. He doesn’t have time to go through all the knowledge he knows about alchemy.
The tower already has access to that, so all he has to do is ask it, and the answer will be provided.

[Yes. Prepare an herbal bath with Moonshade Leaves, Crimson Blossom, and Ground-drake Spiritroot. These will neutralize the venom and accelerate her recovery. You already have these herbs from the ones you purchased for your body tempering.]
"Master, I have a way to cure the cut on your back, but to do that, you would have to take an herbal bath. But..." Kent scratched his head.
"Go on," Saintess Selene prompted, already guessing where he was headed yet still wanting to hear it.
"You would have to take the bath... naked. But don’t worry, Master, I won’t do anything weird to your body, I promise. I just want to cure you," Kent said earnestly.
"Okay. I trust you won’t have any weird ideas," Saintess Selene replied, though a part of her hesitated.
Why?

Because, at this very moment, she wasn’t in the right mindset. She had always prided herself on being someone who didn’t need anyone. However, when faced with life and death, she found herself relying on a man she had never truly acknowledged.
This made her start rethinking everything she believed in. Her cold and aloof personality suddenly seemed to have done her no real good.

But thankfully, she was alive, and she could fight another day. For now, though, she had to heal and to do so, she would have to strip naked before her disciple—a man who had already set his sights on her.
Kent entered the bathroom and filled the tub with water. He then tossed the herbs the tower had suggested into the tub before blinking back into the room.
"I will remove your clothes now, Master," Kent said before loosening the dress covering Saintess Selene’s body.
Soon, the last piece of clothing fell. Kent admired the voluptuous body before him and whistled.
"Although I said I wouldn’t do anything weird, looking at your body, I kind of want to explore it. You wouldn’t mind, would you?" Kent teased.
"If you do anything weird, I will cut your hands off," Saintess Selene commented, her face growing hot.

The body she had been hiding for many years was now fully exposed in front of her one and only shameless disciple, who had promised to make her call him "Master." Instead, he was seeing everything under rather anticlimactic circumstances, to say the least.
"Let’s go," Kent said, taking her in a princess carry and walking toward the bathroom. Once inside, he placed her in the bath, submerging her entire body except for her head in the water.
"Things will get hot, but endure. The moment the poison is out, your wounds will heal," Kent said before summoning his alchemy flame.
He began heating the bath with his alchemy flame.
Soon, the water grew hot and began exuding intense vapour. Saintess Selene, seated in the bath, felt the poison in her body being expelled through the cut on her back.

Most of the poison was gone thirty minutes later, but the water was now boiling. Though she could withstand it, for some reason, she felt an intense heat invade her body and work its way through her system.
An hour later, her eyes grew drowsy, and soon, she lost consciousness.
Two hours later, Kent brought her out of the bath and used a towel to dry her skin. He then carried her to her bed and gently laid her down.
But he didn’t immediately cover her. Kent pressed his palm on the wound on her back, which was finally healing.
The [Blood Void Flame] entered the wound, repairing the damaged tissues. The process took a few minutes before he stopped.
He then scanned her body, his eyes lingering on her perfectly round, soft ass.
Pah!
A gentle slap landed on it, making it jiggle. Kent smiled at the sight, watching the subtle ripple under his touch, and made a mental note.
"I’ll tap that soon," he murmured, covering her with a blanket before leaving the room. He had to find out who attacked her and why.
If the answer had anything to do with the Ashland Family, he would visit them, even if the odds were stacked against him.
Little did he know, a similar fate had already befallen the Ashland Family. Chaos engulfed their estate overnight, and by daybreak, their entire world had turned upside down.
Kent exited the room and headed to the mansion where Cynthia resided. She was the best person to answer his questions.
After he left, Saintess Selene, who was supposed to be sleeping, brushed her hand against the spot on her backside where Kent had slapped her.
"Mmmh..."

A few seconds later, a moan she had been suppressing escaped her lips. Her face flushed beet red as she adjusted her position, ensuring her shameless disciple wouldn’t return to land yet another slap.
She would wake up five days later, and from that moment on, she would realize that holding back wouldn’t work. So, she might as well give in to him.

chapters.title: Chapter 112: The Book of Stories and Legends
paragraphs: Back in the god realm, Vexthra, who hadn’t left the room since Kent jumped into the portal, was sitting with her fists clenched.

Right now, she was waiting for Kent or her sisters to reach out and inform her of the outcome of the attack. Of course, she never expected Kent to contact her since he only had a few seconds left to talk to her, so she was waiting for Unity or Lilian.
It had been almost three hours since Kent left.
"Big sister, can you hear me?" Suddenly, Unity’s voice entered her head, making her smile cutely.
She may be a goddess, but she was powerless when manipulating events in the mortal realm. In fact, she shouldn’t have been able to talk to Kent and her sisters like that.
However, thanks to the tower, she could do it quite easily.
"Unity, is everything alright on your end?" Vexthra asked, like the caring big sister she was.
"Yes, big sister. We are okay," Unity replied.
"Good. It’s great that nothing happened to you two. What about Kent? Is he okay too?" Vexthra asked.
"Yes. He just finished taking care of his master, who was hurt during the battle, but she’s fine now," Unity replied again.
Kent had already informed her that the Saintess was well, so she could tell Vexthra. With only 30 seconds left, he wouldn’t waste time on things like this.
"Can you tell me what happened?" Vexthra asked.

Unity went ahead and narrated everything. Kent had already told her to share everything while he went to talk to Cynthia. He knew Vexthra would be worried, so since she had unlimited time with her sisters, they could manage to a certain extent.
"Wait, what happened to his carriage driver? Is he dead?" Vexthra asked.
"No. Kent saved him. He used some weird way to save him," Unity replied.
"What weird way?" Vexthra asked.
Unity, of course, didn’t immediately reply. She pondered for a moment and then asked Kent.
’Go ahead, tell her everything,’ Kent gave her the go-ahead. Vexthra wouldn’t betray him. She was the one who saved him and brought him this joy he missed out on for 32 years.
Kent trusted her, though, just as he liked his women, so he wasn’t worried.
Unity proceeded to tell her everything. She narrated how Kent had used a token to turn Uncle Drew into a Night Rider.
"Wait, did you just say a Night Rider? Are you sure?" Vexthra asked.
"Yes. From what I heard, Kent referred to him as Kael Duskbane, the captain of the Night Riders," Unity said. "Do you know who that is?" she asked.

"I only know of the stories. Although I am a goddess, I am not a Celestial God, so I don’t know everything. But I will ask around and learn more. For now, make sure you keep a close eye on things for me.
Kent might be strong, but he needs you guys. At the first sign of danger, let me know," Vexthra said before cutting the connection.
She immediately dressed and took an artefact from her soul space.
"Mother, I am coming to visit you. Please grant me passage," Vexthra said before channelling her divine energy into the artefact.
A few seconds later, she vanished.

Somewhere far from the god realm, she appeared in front of a temple that seemed to have aged beyond its limit. However, if one paid close attention, one would realize the temple was made of bones mutating into vines.
It looked both elegant and dangerous.
Vexthra sighed and walked in.

"It’s been how long? 1.4 million years since I last saw you, daughter," immediately upon Vexthra entering the temple, an otherworldly beauty that seemed to surpass Vexthra in all aspects spoke with a loving smile.
She was seated on a bone-like throne, her hair cascading all over. In fact, her hair was so much that it couldn’t be contained in the throne, spilling down onto the jade ground.
"It was you who never wanted to see me, mother. I tried coming multiple times," Vexthra said with a small smile.

The lady looked at her and chuckled. "Hmm. To think a mere mortal was able to knock you up. If your fellow gods learn of this, you will become a laughing stock." The lady’s sweet laughter filled the temple.
"I don’t care. He is my man, and I won’t change anything about what has happened. I love him, and he loves me. That is all I wanted, even without knowing it." Vexthra blushed slightly.
Indeed, if the gods found out, she would become a laughingstock. However, it would undoubtedly make some gods very jealous.
While Vexthra may not be the most beautiful goddess in the Gold Realm, she is undoubtedly one of the most powerful.
A god who wields the power of Hatred and Resentment is undoubtedly one of the most powerful gods. So, getting claimed by a mere mortal was something they would indeed laugh about.
Some, too, would be jealous. After all, both gods and goddesses had tried to court her at one point in time, but she never budged.
"I wish your sister were here to witness," the lady said with a slight sigh.
"Don’t worry, mother. My sister will one day come to us. We just have to wait for the right time," Vexthra said, looking at her mother, who held a sad expression.
Looking closely at her eyes, one can see she wields two sets of eyes.
Although both eyes are ocean blue, the left one seems to contain all the negative emotions in the universe.
Hatred, Resentment, jealousy, envy... All the negative emotions are buried deep in that eye. In fact, looking closely would be enough to tell one she has all those emotions in her.
The right eye, however, contains all the positive emotions. Love, happiness, joy... all the positive emotions are buried in there.
"Why are you here, daughter?" the lady asked.
"I need a copy of the Book of Stories and Legends," Vexthra said, looking directly at the left eye when she spoke. She seemed to be speaking to the left eye.

"You would have to be specific about what you want, daughter. You know, after this, you can’t claim anything again, and asking for the entire book is not possible. So be specific," the lady said, making Vexthra nod.
"I want the pages in the Book of Stories and Legends that detail the Epic Saga of the Riders of The Night. I want every last page," Vexthra made her wish.
"Very well," the lady said, waving her hand. A few seconds later, a stack of pages appeared in her hand, and she gestured for Vexthra to come for it.
"Remember, daughter, the tales of the forgotten are not meant to be disturbed. Once you seek them, they will never leave you. Beware, for the past can return when least expected."
"I will heed your wise words, mother," Vexthra bowed slightly before walking away. Soon, she was back in her realm, where she placed the pages down and started preparing to dive into them later.
Inside the temple, the lady sighed after Vexthra was gone.
"You have made a wise decision, daughter, but are you ready for the sacrifice?"

chapters.title: Chapter 113: What was Stolen
paragraphs: "So, you are telling me your husband was part of the mysterious group that attacked your home and that the spy I caught was the leader of these people?" Kent asked, looking rather shocked.
After leaving his master’s room, Kent came to talk to Cynthia, who was a little shaken by the incident.
After all, hundreds of guards and maids had died in the sudden attack on their home. It was so sudden, in fact, that many died, not even knowing what was happening.
However, what made her mind flip was the fact that the one who had led the attack was her very own husband, who was meant to ensure the safety of their home.
And if that wasn’t bad enough, her husband had tried to kill her and the Saintess. It was mind-boggling, and Kent was completely taken aback by hearing it for the first time.

"Yes. It seems John was under some spell that made him act against his free will," Cynthia said. "As to whether he was pretending or not, I don’t really know. But I know for sure John didn’t act like the John I knew."
"I see. Then can I assume John and the Ashlands are in cahoots?" Kent asked.
Since he had just found out that the spy he caught was the one who had come back and massacred the Alderfords, he could only imagine that he might have been in league with his enemies—the Ashlands.
"I don’t think so. Just an hour ago, a spy we have in the Alderford Mansion reported that Dave Ashland, his wives, and some high-ranking members of the family were assassinated.
From how he described it, it all happened overnight and was only recently discovered," Cynthia replied, making Kent frown.
"Then does this mean that aside from this mysterious group that calls themselves the Hand, there is another organization at work?" Kent asked, immediately feeling a bad premonition.
Somehow, he knew this had something to do with him—or, more importantly, Li Hua.

[Master, I think this is related to the lady you killed at the prison. From the little memory you extracted while blacked out, it appears she belonged to an underworld organization called the Dark Devil Church.
I don’t know much, but we can start with that.]
’Thanks, Tower. Let’s review the memories after this,’ Kent said before returning his gaze back to Cynthia.
"I don’t know if the two incidents are coincidences or connected to the same people, but I know this wasn’t a random attack.
Do you perhaps have any idea what they were after?" Kent asked.

Cynthia nodded. "I think they were after a key. A while back, John returned from one of his many business trips with a key. Back then, he only told me a name and said it would be better if I didn’t know the details of it."
"Now that I think about it, that was also around the same time that scheming bitch came into this family," Cynthia said, her gaze deep in thought.
"What is the name of this Key?" Kent asked.
"It was called the ’Key of Aetherial Flame,’" Cynthia said, her voice barely above a whisper.
"The Key of Aetherial Flame," he repeated.
"Yes. That was the name he told me the last time." Cynthia nodded.

[Master, I believe this is a major issue. In fact, this is a dangerous issue that can’t be discussed now. Finish everything now, and we can talk about it. Also, I have already started looking for the key, but it seems it’s long gone]

"John stored it in the treasury, but an hour ago, when I checked, the key, along with every treasure, was gone. It seems that was what they came for, or maybe they just picked it up after robbing us of everything," Cynthia sighed.
Right now, she was in a difficult spot. Hundreds of her guards and maids were dead, so she had to do something for their families.
Also, now that her family’s foundation was gone, it meant only one thing: total destruction. The only thing she could do was hope to find a way to send them on their way.
But as it stood, she was broke beyond limits.
Millions of spirit stones and all the goods they possess that can be sold for profit had been stolen. Basically, she was penniless at the moment.
"What do you plan on doing next?" Kent asked.
He didn’t need to be a genius to know the lady in front of him was not having an easy time. Her husband had betrayed her and her entire family, causing the deaths of hundreds.

"I will sell the rest of the properties and send the remaining guards and Maids on their way. I will also have to compensate the families of the deceased. After that, I will go back home to see if I can get back on my feet somehow," Cynthia said with a defeated sigh.
Kent shook his head and stood up to leave.
He needed to get things sorted out and leave for the academy. He didn’t find staying in the city safe at the moment.
That was especially true as long as he still hadn’t awakened the Tower. He had to get into the academy and work on that.
"Take this. I believe it will be enough to cover the guards and other expenses. Also, don’t sell the house. Donate it to an orphanage or something.
I will be leaving now to take care of some things. If you need me, you know where to find me."
Kent vanished, leaving Cynthia shocked.
Kent had just dropped a billion spirit stones in her lap and left. That alone was enough to tell her the man who had just left was no ordinary person.
She was so shocked that she didn’t move an inch for the next ten minutes. Only after she regained her senses did she leave to talk to Lilian, her daughter.
Lilian, who hadn’t expected Kent to drop that money on her mother’s lap, giggled when she saw her mom’s face.
"Mom, you already made up your mind, and now that you’re free, you can’t wait any longer.
Give the money to me and go to him. If your performance is worthwhile, he might just make you his woman. After all, how long has it been since you’ve had something enter your body?"
Lilian giggled, taking the pouch of money from her mother. To her, now that John was dead, it was good riddance.
She knew the pain her mother had endured all these years, and now that the source of her pain was headless and burnt to ash, it was time for her to move on.
"I will need a few days," Cynthia said, still looking shocked.
Lilian sighed and stood to leave. "Just don’t take too long, Mom. Unity is talking to him now, and since I already know the answer, you shouldn’t waste too much time."
She left to take care of her family. She knew her family was done for her but didn’t care. She is now Kent’s woman. The Alderford can go screw themselves.
Cynthia lay on her bed and started contemplating what she had to do. In the end, she chose to follow her heart’s desire.
If only she knew that, in the coming months, she would experience the best times she had ever had in her entire life.

chapters.title: Chapter 114: Keys Of The Apocalypse
paragraphs: After Kent returns to his room, he begins digesting everything with the tower. A lot is happening, and he needs to understand it since things could go bad very soon.
"So, we have two secret organizations now: the Dark Devil Church and the Hand. Are they perhaps related or in competition with each other?" Kent wondered.
[I don’t think they are the same, Master. From her memory, I learnt they don’t want anyone to know their business and thus use binding contracts to operate.
Of course, the memory I have is that of a lower ranker. But still, it contains more than enough information to help you draw some conclusions,] the tower chimed in.
"Right. Tower, for now, go through the memory and give me the key information I will need to gauge the danger level. I don’t believe these people are done," Kent instructed.
Although he hated the idea of not being the one to bring down the Ashland family, he had to be the one to investigate.

The reason was simple. Lilian and Li Hua were the threads tying them together. He knew if these hidden assassins found this connection, they would, without a doubt, come after the Platinum Spirit Root, which is Lilian and the Atomic Divine Body.
Without a doubt, the assassins would know he was linked to them and would soon come after him if they hadn’t already.
This was why he needed to determine the best course of action.

Since he doesn’t have enough soul and mental strength to hold the memories he has absorbed, he can rely on the tower to handle them. This way, he wouldn’t have to worry about losing valuable information.
[Master, I have finished scanning through the memories.]
"Go ahead, tell me what I need to know."
[After scanning the memories, I found some interesting points. The first is that the Dark Devil Church is terrifying, and this is based on the memories of someone with Tier 3-level authority.
From her memories, the church operates with four Tiers. The first is their leader, the highest authority in their branch. Of course, she suspected there would be a big boss above them.
However, this leader is the highest authority in her knowledge. According to her memories, this leader is halfway through the Root Transcendent stage—the stage after Root’s Great Sage.
Tier 2 consists of the Root Great Sages known as City Lords. These individuals manage the church’s operations at the city level.
Tier 3 is where she was before her death. Her role was to scout for talents that could be trained or stolen from to fund their research. All Tier 3 members are in the Root Sage stage.

Lastly, there is Tier 4, which includes their soldiers and other workers. From what she knows, this stage includes individuals down to the Root Grandmaster level. That seems to be their limit; they do not go below that level.
Additionally, she has single-handedly ensured that over a dozen people lost their Spirit Roots, which I believe they are using to create powerful subordinates.]
"Well, this is bad, isn’t it?" Kent said.

[Indeed. But the master shouldn’t worry. Per my calculations, you will step into the Grandmaster stage in just a week of active cultivation and activate the towers. For now, you don’t have to worry much.]
"I know, buddy, but a Root Transcendent is something way out of my league." Kent didn’t need a genie to tell him he was in for a wild one.
If a Root Transcendent were to come after him, his life would be in danger.
[That is true, but the master is underestimating me. I have to let the master know my sole purpose is to ensure your safety, and so far, I have been doing that.

The master may not know yet, but the towers that have been awakened are a major part of your strength. However, the moment they are fully unlocked and accessible will be when you understand what a gift you have.
Without me fully unlocked, your bloodline is still akin to a dormant bloodline. But with me fully awakened, you will understand more.]
"Thanks for reminding me, Tower. I’m just frustrated right now, not being there for my master and wives when they needed me," Kent sighed.
[The master doesn’t have to worry. With you gaining enough women in your harem, you will understand that you are not alone in this enterprise.
As you know, the more ladies you have, the stronger your soul. Soon, you will understand what this means.]

"Okay, I guess I won’t waste much time now. I need to add more women I can play with every day," Kent said with a smile. Vexthra had already nagged him for being petty, so this time, Kent wanted to go wild.
"However, Tower, we already know something about the Church, but nothing about the Hand," Kent stated.
[Indeed. However, we now know they are after a key they have already acquired. Now, before you say anything, I only know a little about the key, and I must say, it’s a nasty thing.]
"Tell me, Tower."

[The Key of Aetherial Flame is one of the Seven Keys of Pandorax. I don’t know much, mainly because I am still not fully awakened, but I do know the Pandorax is an ancient box said to contain the Key of the Apocalypse.
This means that this key is one of the seven keys, and when the seven keys of the Pandorax box are gathered, they can open it and unleash the apocalypses.
Now, before you think I’m speaking nonsense, know that the Key of the Apocalypse is said to have the power to open the gate of the apocalypse and unleash the Race of Apocalypse upon this world.
I don’t know why these people are after the key, but I have two pieces of advice for the master.
First, unlock the Tower and use it to grow stronger quickly. And second, hurry to reach the peak and ascend before all the keys are found.
Trust me, when the apocalypse is unleashed on this world, you can consider it finished.]
"Damn, that is one nasty thing. I’ll take your advice, Tower. The faster I leave this world, the better for me," Kent said, determined. However, destiny had other plans for him.
[Master, I know you don’t want to stick your divine rod just anywhere, but it would be best if you assumed the role of a full-time dual cultivator.
You need to grow stronger. The apocalypse is not something to joke about, and I wouldn’t want the master or his ladies caught up in it.]

"I will, Tower. You don’t have to worry too much about that. I’ll make sure my women and I are out of this world before all seven keys are found," Kent sighed, firm in his resolve. However, the universe had other ideas.

<Do you want to accept? Y/N>
<Failure to accept will bring upon you a great punishment. Punishment: Your dick will stop working for three years. You have five days to accept. Make the wise choice.>

chapters.title: Chapter 116: Black Dahlia Inn
paragraphs: Black Dahlia Inn is one of the many inns in the kingdom of Athea, where the underworld often meets. It’s their safe haven.

It is said that when a criminal enters this place, not even the king can force them out, as doing so would expose the underworld to the entire world, which will incur their wrath on whoever dares expose them.
Of course, there are only a few knew of this shady place, but to the criminals, this place is their haven—the only place they feel at home and free from all kinds of trouble.
Inside this inn, dozens of people could be seen doing all kinds of things people do in inns. Some were drinking, chatting, eating, and so on.
"Have you heard? The Ashland and Alderford families seem to have offended somebody they shouldn’t have," a figure in black said to his friends.
"I know, right? To have your entire family wiped from the face of the world... who had the Ashland family offended to meet this fate?" another commented.

"You’re asking the wrong question," another chimed in. "Since the Ashland family is a noble family, who and what has the audacity to go after them? I know we all have our issues with them, but going against an entire noble family... That is just—"

"Maybe the two families were in cahoots with someone they shouldn’t have messed with. I mean, although the Alderford merchant family isn’t that widely known, it’s still one of the top five families in Caprath City.
Maybe they bit off more than they could chew, and it choked them in ways they never expected," a new person joined in on the conversation.
"You all might be wrong," another person, a young man clad in dark green clothes with a hood covering his face, said from the corner.
"What do you mean?" the first person to speak asked.
"Can’t you all see it? One died overnight from a silent assassination, and another died from extreme combat. I don’t think the same people are after them. This might just be a big coincidence."
It had been 12 hours since the incident with the Alderford family. And since both incidents involving the Ashland and Alderford families were identical, everyone called them the same.
The underworld was also calling them the same. They all believed the same fate had befallen both families.
However, they were all wrong. The incident wasn’t something anyone could easily comprehend.
The reason was simple: the two incidents stemmed from two different factions of the underworld, a revelation that would soon ignite conflict between them.
Inside a private room in the inn, three figures—whose presence alone identified them as significant underworld members—could be seen sipping wine.
"What do you all think? Do you believe there’s a new force trying to sabotage us?" the first man asked.
These three were the Root Great Sages sent by the Dark Devil Church to investigate Lady Sandra’s death and the sudden appearance of the Atomic Divine Body.
They had arrived two days ago and immediately interrogated the Ashland noble family.
However, Daisy and Dave had lied to them and manipulated the situation, redirecting their attention to the Makoso Prison, where they discovered the mutilated remains of one of their members.
This discovery enraged them, so they immediately returned to the Ashland family estate. Overnight, they slaughtered dozens of its members, including Dave and his wives.

The reason for this swift retribution was simple: one of the sages possessed a strange ability to discern lies. In truth, it was as though he could read minds. Because of this, Daisy’s carefully crafted scheme was stopped overnight.
However, after killing every last one of them, they failed to discover any information about the Atomic Divine Body. They had already killed all those who knew anything about it.
Still, they were aware of the connection between the Ashlands and the Alderfords, so they moved to investigate the latter.
But that was when they witnessed the one-sided massacre of the Alderfords by an organization that called itself the Hand.
In fact, while they were in hiding, they saw how the group entered and came out within ten minutes before vanishing entirely.
Witnessing this, they decided to assess the situation and understand what was happening before making any subtle moves.
So they waited for four hours after the battle, and just as the sky was turning dark, they prepared to make their move.
However, something strange happened before they could get within 20 meters of the Alderford Mansion.
A portal opened, and a hooded figure on a dark, eerie horse appeared. Within a minute, this figure slaughtered four Root Sages and six Root Saints.
The three Root Great Sages fled in a panic, abandoning their men. In fact, they left everything behind and bolted. Since then, they have holed up inside Black Dahlia to re-strategize.
"I think there is a new force at play. The fact that they were able to unleash that kind of power to subdue the Merchants means they are a force we can’t ignore," one of them said.

"I think we should hurry back. Although the Atomic Divine Body is important, a new faction in the underworld that can command such strength threatens us. The leader must be informed," the third person added.
"I mean, the fact that they noticed us and even sent that figure on the horse tells us everything we need to know."
After the incident, they immediately linked the dark-hooded figure to the strange organization known as The Hand.
"We have to retreat for now. We must inform the leader, and this can’t be done over communication crystals. We’ll have to abandon the pursuit of the Atomic Divine Body for now.
This new threat must be addressed first."
And so, the three figures abandoned their mission to pursue the Atomic Divine Body, at least for now.

Had it not been for such a fatal blow from the dark-hooded figure, they would have continued their search for the Atomic Divine Body and likely stumbled upon Li Hua, whose unique nature would have undoubtedly piqued their curiosity.
Fortunately, Kent’s First Rider, the captain of the Night Riders, intervened before they could act.

They were utterly terrified when Uncle Drew made his appearance. Because of this, Kent, who would have been backed into a corner, now had a few more days to take care of matters before everything turned upside down.
The three figures left and headed to their headquarters to report the recent developments.

Meanwhile, three days after the incident involving the Alderford and Ashland families, the twelve major merchant families from the twelve cities in the Athea Kingdom convened to discuss their next course of action.
Now that a noble family had fallen, they needed to select a replacement.
In fact, this was an outcome many had been waiting for years to see. Each family wanted to ascend to the rank of nobility, but none had dared to challenge the Ashlands directly due to their power.
However, the situation had changed. One could inherit the Ashland businesses and their army if they played their cards right.
This was the rule set by the king: if a merchant family manages to inherit a noble family’s position, they take everything the noble family owns.
And so, the twelve families were all vying to become the next Lords of Caprath City.
