I don’t mind, and it’ll be good to have my precious world here in my domain.
It’ll help me remember my past and where I came from."
Though he couldn’t return to Earth just yet, he knew that in a few years, he would be able to.
For now, he had more important things to use the compass for than going back to Earth for revenge.
He had made peace with his death.
However, if he ever got his hands on those who killed him, he would love nothing more than to torture them.
Now that he has the tower prison, he can bring them back with him and continue torturing them tell they grow old and die.
When he appeared in front of the Tower, a golden light beam descended on him like a futuristic teleporter.
He was sucked into the tower.
Well, a Bifrost bridge would be a more accurate name for what the tower had cooked up—just that his own was golden in color instead of multicolored.
[Welcome to the Tower, Master.
As you can see, this place is the admin room.
You have access to everything, but to make it much more fun, I created this room, which I will be the only one to use anyway.
But I just wanted to show you.
I hope you like it.]
Kent stared at the screens, which showed some of the important towers in the room.
On one screen, a pink tower named Harem is plastered on it.
Others displayed Sword, Servant, Guardian, Alchemy, Soul, and Legion.
But those weren’t the only screens there.
There were others with their names displayed on them:
Tower City, Tower Shop, Tower Storage, Tower Prison.
The place was just too disturbing in a way, but Kent knew the Tower just wanted to have fun.
He didn’t care—as long as she played her role well, they wouldn’t have a problem.
"Say, Tower, can you change your form when I’m around?" Kent asked.
Having a tower following him was cute but, in a way, disturbing.
[Sure.]
Like she said, she could indeed take other forms, and she did.
The Tower glowed, and in the next second, a cute little fairy appeared.
Kent felt uncomfortable in a way, but that feeling was wiped away when a bandana appeared around her head, and then a bandit hat sat on top of that.
Her small wings also turned transparent, and like a pirate, she smiled at Kent, making him wonder whether he should tell her to change again.
But he did not.
Whatever makes her happy.
Vexthra did say the Tower is sentient.
"Take me to the Tower Shop," Kent said.
"Aye, Captain!" she replied with a cheeky grin, crossing her tiny arms.
"Follow me, and we’ll plunder the finest treasures this shop o’ yours has to offer, arr!"
Kent wanted to give her a slap, but she was just too tiny, with no surface area to slap.
But once again, whatever makes her happy.
They vanished, and the next second, they appeared in a room filled with smaller screens, each displaying an image of something.
Kent immediately approached a screen that was showing a skill book.
He looked at the screen that displayed its name, grade, rank and description, and Price.
[Name: Infinity Piercing Arrow]
[Grade: Heaven]
[Rank: SSS]
-- Conjure an arrow that travels with speed 50 times faster.
-- Conjuring time reduces as more arrows are being fired.
-- Consumes 100 Spiritual qi per arrow.
[Price: 340,000 Tower Points]
"Not bad, not bad at all.
I like this shop room," Kent said, smiling after reading through more than twenty screens.
It reminded him of online shopping back on Earth.
"Gaia, can you make a screen similar to this in any room of my choosing?
It would be best to have a screen where I and my women can browse through the store."
[That won’t be a problem.
But the master must know that some items can’t be accessed just yet since most will be added as you grow stronger.
For now, you have access up to the Divine grade.]
"That’s not an issue.
I don’t need skill books for now anyway." Kent loved the shop room.
Hundreds of skill books, weapons, clothes, armor, and other treasures could benefit anyone.
"Gaia, you mentioned me needing to buy some talismans to speed up the absorption rate of soul essence from the bead."
[Yes.
But since the master will be using the Soul Tower, buying them wouldn’t be of much use.]
"I see.
In that case, give me my two rewards before I forget.
Also, you should reward my ladies and the ones to come.
On Earth, in some countries, there’s something called a grand opening sale.
It’s where your first ten customers, after opening a store, are given items for free."
Kent grinned like a bandit.

chapters.title: Chapter 131: Call of the Legend and Myth
paragraphs: In a sense, the tower was meant to give him everything for free anyway. But that would just be bland. It would also make the existence of tower points useless.

So he needed that. But that also didn’t mean the tower had to be strict with him. If a Heaven-grade skill book was selling for less than a million tower points, it could only mean the tower didn’t take much.

Or perhaps tower points, in a way, were equivalent to billions of spirit stones. But he wasn’t sure if that was the point. So he could only focus on what he could get for free first before spending money.
[The master is lying to me, but I will make an exception. Of course, I will not hand you ten items for free. There should be a catch. Do you want to know?]
"Fire away, Gaia." Kent knew for a fact the tower was meant to make him stronger. So whatever it did, it wasn’t an excuse—it was a way to make him grow.

[The master will receive ten free items if he can make his master his woman within the next three weeks. If you do it in two, I will double it. If within a week, I will triple it and even throw in a True Name Token.]
"Deal," Kent smiled. He knew his master was as good as his. Why? Because she wanted him but was too shy to make a move.
But now that there were loads of things on the line, he wouldn’t let the woman suffer anymore. He would help her release some of her pent-up stress.
[Here are your two rewards. One is precious for your legion tower, so treasure it.]
Kent received two items. He immediately appraised it. Now that the tower has awakened, his appraising abilities have also become several times more powerful.
[One Time Purchase Pass]
-- Gaia thanks the master for awakening him faster than expected. Gaia would allow the master to buy anything for free using this card.
-- The master doesn’t need to thank me. I am meant to keep all these things safe for him anyway.
-- But the master can thank me if he wants because Gaia understands the importance of emotions to humans and living things.
"Thank you, Gaia," Kent said with a smile, making the pirate fairy smile. That is what sentient beings can do. They are more than emotionless machines. No, they function just like humans.

Kent put the card away since he would have to take his time to go around and inspect all the items here before he could say for sure what he wanted to get. He has two days to do that. But even if he couldn’t do that now, he could return later.
He took the next item. Surprisingly, this is a portal item.
[Name: Call of the Legend and Myth]
[Grade: Spirit Grade (Soul Item)]
[Type: Summoning & Portal]

-- In legends and myths, some brave individuals, lost to history, fought to fend off evil and save their homes and kin. They were the brave warriors of myth, those whose legends were swallowed by time.
-- Some were good individuals with morals, fighting to protect their homes out of a sense of duty.
-- Some were evil, battling other evils. Out of necessity, they fought to protect those they chose to shield and died defending them.
-- These brave souls are meant to be remembered. They are the legends of old myths, the lost ones—those forgotten by time.

-- But it is said that the lost ones, those swept away by the stream of time, those forgotten by history, will rise again and march under one banner with a single purpose: to protect those who cannot protect themselves.
<Summoning>
-- When the stars align, and the constellations follow suit, the owner of this item can summon these legends lost in the stream of time—those whose stories have been forgotten.
-- One summon at a time.
-- The owner will know their names and call them forth when the fabric of time is torn.
-- All those summoned will wholeheartedly obey the orders of the master (Owner).
-- All those summoned, if they lack one, can inherit true names that will automatically be bestowed upon them as gratitude for their roles in shaping the universe.
<Portal>
-- The universe bled when some of these legends fell. Some fell due to betrayal, some died due to odds stacked against them, and some fell due to empty promises.
-- These legends don’t deserve their ending. They deserve a much better ending.
-- That is why the universe will grant the owner, brave enough to travel through time and space, the chance to save these legends and bring them back to continue their legacies.
[Note: If the owner dies in those strange times, he will be teleported back to the tower, where he will enter a comatose state for a year, depending on the cause of death.]
[Does the master want to form a soul contract with this item?]
"Let’s do it, Gaia." Kent, for some reason, was very happy. In fact, it wouldn’t be an exaggeration to say he was beyond happy.
For some reason, reading that some of these lost legends could be saved, he wanted nothing more than to go back in time or forward in time to save them.
The feeling was that he needed to do it. He wanted to do it, and for a moment, his soul and heart agreed on the same thing.
He would become the ferryman of time and space. Someone who ferries lost legends—those legends of myth. Those who need to be remembered.
[The master has formed a soul contract with this item. From now on, when there is a chance, the master will know and summon these legends.
Also, when the universe wills it, the master will receive a quest telling you where to go and when to save these brave warriors.]
"Thank you, Gaia." Kent smiled and then explored the Shop for a while, ensuring he got a general idea of things he had access to and their prices.
After a while, he realizes he needs to earn loads of Tower points if he wants to buy anything good from the tower.

(A/N: I’m leaving this here for all my readers. You can drop the names of any legends you feel deserve saving. I’ll research them and find a way to bring them into the story [a nice gift might help speed up the process... Lol].

Regarding summoning, it will usually take up to three Chapters to execute. This is because I want to show their moments leading up to the summoning. I don’t want to randomly introduce a character and then spend time later explaining their backstory.
I’ll delve into most of their backstories before they are summoned. This ensures these legends are properly represented and get their share of screen time before the chaos ends.
As for the portal (Ferryman), it will take between 5–10 Chapters since the MC will need to travel to those distant times.
There will be twists and turns, but I promise to pull off every last ferry like my life depends on it [well, your gifts, power stones, and Golden Tickets sure do].
That’s all for now. Again, drop the name of your legend, and I’ll make it happen.
You can reach me on Discord: pen_drop.)

chapters.title: Chapter 132: The Sword Tower
paragraphs: "So, a True Name token is 20 million Tower points? What a cheat," Kent said, staring at the section housing the True Name tokens.
He had hoped to buy at least two—to use on Unity and Lilian—but seeing the price now, Kent couldn’t understand why he’d even bothered to look.

[I think the master should know there are no free meals in this life. You have to work for it. But since I am such a benevolent seller, I will throw in a 30% discount for the sake of all the transactions we will have in the future.]
"You’re a huge scammer, Gaia. In fact, where did all these things even come from, anyway?" Kent laughed at Gaia’s shamelessness.
[The master shouldn’t worry about where these items came from. Even I don’t know. The only thing I know is assigning prices and figuring out ways to improve them for the master.]
"I see. I guess I’ll have to work harder to earn more Tower points and buy some for them," Kent muttered, recalling how much the True Name had benefited Uncle Drew. He wanted the same for his lovers.

[The master shouldn’t worry. You will receive more quests to help you earn the points. Now that I’ve awakened, the chances of your ladies automatically gaining True Names are quite high. But for now, don’t depend on that.]
[Instead, you should focus on the lady in your bed. For some reason, I sense something incredibly good and powerful emanating from her. In fact, you should hurry and add her to the harem.]
Kent nodded and explored the store for a while before leaving for the Sword Tower.
The moment he arrived, he was greeted by the sight of a tall sword embedded in the ground.
The sword’s surface bore markings that Kent recognized within a minute as the 10,002 sword plays he was mastering to become a True Swords Master.

However, that wasn’t all he noticed. Beyond the markings, there was a potent energy emanating from the sword. His sword qi and intent reacted immediately, and intriguingly, he could feel his body beginning to absorb it.
"Gaia, what is this sword, and why do I feel like I should bow to it?" Kent asked, sensing the commanding respect the energy exuded.

[It’s called the Sword of Enlightenment. What you’re feeling is what most call Sword Will. It is the last stage of swordsmanship and the path to transcending to the pinnacle of every swordsman’s dreams] Gaia replied.
"And where is that?" Kent’s blood began to boil with excitement.
[One with the Sword. It’s the pinnacle of swordsmanship. Throughout history, only 22 people have ever reached that level. In fact, even the current god of the sword has not achieved it.]
Kent felt his excitement surge at the thought of reaching such heights. Currently, he is a Pseudo Swords Master with both sword qi and sword intent at the Enhanced Stage.

From what he had learned from Gaia and Vexthra, he would need to transcend nine levels in the Enhanced Stage before ascending to Profound Sword Qi and Intent. After that, he would reach Heavenly Sword Intent and Grand Sword Qi.

That was when he would begin to witness the true essence of swordsmanship. Of course, Kent understood that saying and doing were vastly different things, but the thought of the journey ahead filled him with exhilaration.

"Gaia, although I don’t mean to belittle this sword, isn’t the Sword Will coming from it a little weak?" Kent asked. Based on what he knew, the full force of true Sword Will should have been overwhelming, perhaps even deadly.
[The master is amusing. What you’re feeling isn’t even a sliver of true Sword Will. In fact, this is merely the afterimage of the millionth shadow of true Sword Will.
The current sword is here solely to aid the master’s growth. You shouldn’t expect to encounter the real thing until after you’ve formed your Sword Heart,] Gaia explained.
"Sword Heart?" Kent queried.
[Sword Heart is a stage in swordsmanship where your heart and that of the sword become one. It is the foundational stage for ascending to Sword Will and, ultimately, One with the Sword.
It’s where most swordsmen become stuck. At this stage, you begin to comprehend the Sword Dao, which tests your dedication to the sword and the sword alone.
Many falter here, unable to continue on the path of the sword. You don’t need to worry about it; you’re far from that stage.]
"I see. Swordsmanship is more fun than I thought. I guess I’ll enjoy it even more," Kent said with a smile, knowing any swordsman would smack him silly for such a casual statement.
The path of weapon cultivation was arduous, yet Kent found it exhilarating. Still, success depended on one’s understanding and willingness to dedicate their very soul to it.
"Gaia, aside from the Genesis Path, how many paths are there?" Kent asked, thinking of someone special.
[There are 21 others besides the Genesis Path. Of course, there are others, but they didn’t reach the peak of swordsmanship, so they aren’t worth considering,] Gaia replied.
"I see. Then can I ask where I can obtain any of these 21?"
[The master is already thinking of his master. Perhaps the master should make her his first before planning her future,] Gaia teased with a giggle.
"Yeah, well, you can never be too prepared," Kent muttered, blushing slightly.

Like Vexthra told him, his women were his secret army. He had to ensure they were stronger and well-protected. The fact that he had the tower didn’t mean he could be complacent and think he was invincible.
With him now unknowingly becoming the son of the universe, he had to understand that his life wouldn’t be easy. Having the best and most powerful women by his side was good.
[The master shouldn’t worry. With me now awakened, I will start searching, and the moment I find one, I will do everything I can to obtain it.]
"Thank you, Gaia," Kent sighed, knowing there was a chance.
He was about to move toward the sword when something flashed before his eyes. He quickly checked, only to see something he never expected.
He had received a quest, and perhaps the universe was bored, so it had decided to simultaneously make things much more fun and interesting.
It was as if she wanted Kent to create a scene for her to watch. The quest was shameless, but the rewards were heavenly.
[Ding! You have received a Quest from the Universe.]
[Quest Name: Arrogance Is a Path Too]
[Quest Type:] Single
[Quest Difficulty:] Very High
[Quest Description:]
-- Become a True Swords Master.
-- Join the Sword Gate of the Divine Palace Sect as an Inner Disciple.
-- Once accepted, arrogantly challenge 100 swordsmen in the Inner Sect Area and win all 100 battles.
-- Display your arrogance proudly, showing everyone that a new swordsman has arrived and is here to stay.
-- Be prepared to gather enemies—this is the path of swordsmanship. Face it with courage and resolve, and do not run crying to your master.
[Rewards:]
-- 100,000 Tower Points
-- Heaven Ascendence Sword Path (5th Sword Path)
-- A True Name Token

chapters.title: Chapter 133: Alchemy Tower
paragraphs: [It looks like we wouldn’t have to look too far. All the master has to do is walk into an arena and shout, "Hey losers, I heard y’all hating on me because I became the sole disciple of the Sword Saintess. Well, it’s not my fault you’re losers. If you disagree, you can challenge me. If you win, I’ll drop my status as the disciple of the Sword Saintess."]
Gaia giggled, making Kent’s face twitch. But he couldn’t deny her words; everyone would want to challenge him when they found out the Saintess had a disciple.
That would give him hundreds of challenges to cleave through.

"You’re right, Gaia; I’ll do it like that. This is a rare chance for me to become famous and show everyone I qualify to be the disciple of the Sword Saintess," Kent said with a smile before leaving to check out the other features.
The first place he visited was the Eternal Sword Arena.
What he saw was more like a futuristic dojo. The tower truly meant it when she said the tower world she created would resemble modern Earth. Kent actually liked it.
The structure was made of glass, and just looking at it made one want to step inside. Inside, though, it felt like a world of its own, with customizable settings to suit any preference.
For now, Kent didn’t pay much attention to it since he was just looking around, but Gaia made sure the arena provided a relaxing experience while training inside.

After that, he went to the next place, the Enlightenment Stone, where, as he had expected, there was a pretty large stone sitting under an oak tree. His senses heightened the moment he stepped on it, and his body calmed down.
It wasn’t an exaggeration to say that, aside from practicing in front of the Sword of Enlightenment, the Stone of Enlightenment was the next best thing.

After that, he went to the [Sword Dream] space. Surprisingly, it took the form of an immortal cave. When he asked Gaia, she said it was a real thing picked from somewhere in the universe many years ago.

The moment he stepped in, he felt drowsy, as though he were being pulled into a dream. He immediately stepped out and promised only to enter when he wanted to experience the dreamlike realms where he could witness legendary swordsmen at work.

After that, he went to the last place, the [Perfect Sword View]. This place was similar to the Sword Dream space, but here, he could simply use Gaia to watch, like a VR simulation, the true nature of a sword skill or technique.
He used it to check the Elemental Lord’s skill. What he saw shocked him. If his mastery rose to its peak, a single swing of his sword could conjure a 1,000-meter-tall monster of his choosing.
He planned to use that space well. He even asked if other skills could be checked there, and the answer was yes. So his ladies could also use it.
Afterward, he left for the Alchemy Tower.
The moment he appeared there, the smell of pills and herbs assaulted his nostrils, bringing a smirk to his lips. Of course, he liked the smell; that was all he would be inhaling in the years to come.
He quickly moved to the first feature inside the Alchemy Tower.
"That is one good-looking pill room you made there, Gaia," Kent said with a smile, admiring the cute jade pill room the tower had created.
It was made of black obsidian stones and jade. The exterior alone made the place very attractive. Kent entered, and as he expected, the inside felt like a world of its own.
There was also a cauldron sitting in the room, which revealed itself to be a Legendary-grade pill cauldron after he used his appraisal skills to check.

It was a pretty good furnace, far better than the Rare-grade one he was using. He wanted to take it away, but the tower explained that it was connected to the Tower’s storage, so he could summon it even when he was outside.
He left and went to the Alchemy Garden. He was shocked to discover there were also some herbs growing there. He was very happy about discovering something so good.
But he quickly realized they were all the herbs in his possession. It seemed the tower had taken them from his storage and planted them.

Still, seeing so many herbs growing at such a fast pace seemed surreal yet strikingly awesome. Ten days inside the garden equaled only a minute outside, so the rate at which the herbs were growing was almost visible.
Of course, if he wanted to increase the speed, he could simply feed the garden some beast cores or their bodies. That would add more energy to the garden and hasten the growth.
He also found out the Alchemy Garden could upgrade the tiers of herbs. Alchemy determines the grade of pills by the tier of the herbs used.
Tier 1 herbs can be used for Tier 1 pills. Of course, there are techniques to upgrade Tier 1 pills made from Tier 1 herbs to Tier 2 pills, but only if necessary.
The easiest way, however, was to use Tier 2 herbs for Tier 2 pills. Having a garden that could upgrade Tier 1 herbs to Tier 2.

Naturally, herbs upgrade on their own over time. However, they would need to reach a certain age to do so. But in his case, if he managed to add more energy to the garden, he could grow herbs that would soon upgrade to higher tiers easily.
After he was done exploring the garden, he went to the last place, the [Pill World]. It was similar to the Sword Dream.
This place also pulled one into a dreamlike state, where they would experience the world of Alchemy in ways that transcended common sense.
"Gaia, I’ve been meaning to ask, but are there paths for other weapons?" It was a stupid question, but he asked anyway.
[Yes. There are paths for it. In fact, most True Names come with a path they can walk. Just like your Night Rider, who follows a unique cultivation path.
So, while there are paths for the way of the sword, there are also paths for other weapons. The bow, spear, saber, and others have their own paths.

If you are concerned about your ladies, you won’t have to. The cultivation techniques given to them by the goddess are more than enough. Of course, if they are lucky, their True Name awakening will usher them into a new cultivation phase.]
"Thanks, Gaia." Kent took in the Alchemy Tower for a while before leaving for the Harem Tower, where he planned to spend most of his time with his ladies.
Meanwhile, outside, Saintess Selene returned from her little trip and locked herself in her room. She didn’t want to see Kent at the moment.
The events that had transpired made it difficult for her to think rationally, and she feared that she would make a mistake if she saw Kent right now.
Luckily for her, she fell asleep a few minutes after she returned, and it would last for four hours. That would be when her problems would begin again.
Since Kent was ensuring his master was taken care of, he would be sure to take care of her first. After all, there were no free meals in the world.

chapters.title: Chapter 134: Rise and Ride With Me
paragraphs: Varyndor, the second strongest kingdom in the human continent, is known to have some of the best and most powerful factions and guilds.

There are the Alchemy Guild, Hunters Guild, and many others that comprise a variety of professions and ways of life. In Varyndor, if you are a cultivator and want to earn handsomely, the best way forward is to form a team and join a guild.

Aria is a young lady who specializes in archery. In fact, she is one of the best archers in the city of Stonehaven. She is a member of Eagle Eye Hunters, and due to how much she contributes to the team, many of her teammates respect her.
She is an orphan and a lively one. She ran away from many orphanage homes and chose the life of the wild instead.
With silver hair and blue eyes coupled with her hourglass figure, even heirs from noble and merchant families have their eyes on her.

"Aria, the leader said we will be going to the Demon Mountains today. He said a new treasure has been discovered, and most teams will be going to try their hands at obtaining it," a young lady who had just escaped her teenage days said with a cute little smile.
"Alright, Melody, I will come as soon as I am done. For now, let me rest a little," Aria said, making the young lady pout.

This young lady is practically her sister. She used to follow Aria from one orphanage home to the next, so when she chose the life of the wild, she followed her, and Aria took care of her until she came of age.

"Sleepyhead," Melody said before standing up. "Also, Thane, the second heir of the Malric family, will be going too with his team. I heard he has been keeping an eye on you of late. You better be careful. I won’t be able to shield you from all of them."
"Go away, Melody. I am sleeping." Melody chuckled and left.
Aria is a beauty, so when it comes to catching the eye of most youngsters and thirsty, she doesn’t pale in comparison to some of the ladies from these noble families.

Time went by, and a while later, Aria the Eagle Eye Hunters, comprising 21 members, headed out to the Demon Mountains where a herb had been discovered, and it’s said to be somewhere in the Demon Mountain.
From time to time, people who specialize in locating rare herbs will have something of a premonition, which, in a way, sounds weird, but 100% of the time, they will be right.
Of course, it was mostly because they didn’t know where it was exactly, so they gave a general location and let the lucky teams fight over it.
The Eagle Eye Hunters are no different. They went after most herbs like this, which sell for thousands, if not millions, of spirit stones.

"Aria, you will take care of support when a fight happens. We want our best archer watching our backs. If something is wrong, make sure to grab the herb and run. We don’t want to miss out on this chance to change our lives."
The leader of the eagle eye hunters said while the road was on their mounts. Aria was riding on a beast that looked like a combination of a horse and an antilop.
It has cute little legs and a horn that seems to come from a very powerful bloodline of a spirit beast. It’s the fastest mount in their team.
"What the..." Aria shouted as they gazed at the herb that had appeared on a certain peak. It wasn’t just them. Some other teams were also there.
"Its actually a Ten Year Old Gold Essense Mushroom. We are rich," Most started shouting as they gazed at the herb on the mountain.
It’s a one-of-a-kind herb that when Alchemists get their hands on, they will be able to concoct crazy pills that will sell for millions of spirit stones.
However, it’s guarded by a spirit beast that is at the Root Great Sage stage. But it will be dead soon, considering the number of teams coming after it.
"Aria, the moment we engage in combat, grab the herb and leave with melody. You two have the fastest mountains in the team. The moment we get this to the Alchemy guild, its ours."
Aria nodded and prepared to execute her mission to the best of her abilities.
"Get them!"
Someone shouted as Aria grabbed the herb and made a beeline, speeding away with Melody laughing and giggling behind her.
Within seconds, they were gone, and the fight against the spirit beast, which had just lost its precious herb, went berserk and started attacking with ferocity.
"Everyone scatter. We meet back in Stonehaven," the leader of Aria’s team shouted before he sped away, following the direction Aria and Melody had gone.
The others also went their way, and as the leader had said, they would meet back in the city. That’s how they usually ran their missions when they involved many teams.
"Aria, let’s wait up here for the leader," Melody said as they sped away, keeping miles between them and the fight.
"The leader said we should take it to the alchemy guild, so let’s do that first," Aria said, but Melody insisted they wait for the leader, fearing they would be cheated.
Hearing her sound reasoning, Aria chose to listen to her and wait, as they mostly did sometimes on missions.
Aria stopped at one of their checkpoints and dismounted her mount. Melody did the same and stood beside Aria while waiting for their leader.
But that didn’t happen. A few minutes into the wait, when Aria turned to look in the direction they came from, a pain stabbed from her back, piercing her heart.
She immediately coughed blood and turned to look at what happened. There, she saw Melody stabbing a dagger through her back, a smile filled with hate spreading across her lips.
"W-why?" Aria asked. She couldn’t think of anything but to ask that.

"Don’t blame her, Aria. You aren’t the only one getting the attention of every young heir. My dear Melody here caught my eye, and as the heir of the Malric noble family, I have to make her feel loved.
You had all the attention.
It’s your fault for being so nonchalant about your beauty and not choosing a man. Perhaps that would have calmed my dear Melody’s jealousy. But alas, here we are."
Aria coughed blood and asked again. "W-why?" She couldn’t believe the one she trusted and took care of would backstab her. But alas, it was already too late.

"Let’s go, Melody. I heard the annual auction is a month away. This will sell well. I’ve already made provisions with my family, and they will take us to the Althea kingdom for a while while we put this on auction."
Their leader, now revealed as the aloof heir of the Malric noble family, delivered a stab to Aria’s mount, killing it immediately. Melody flinched but didn’t do anything.

"Okay, leader—I mean, Darrel." Aria watched as Melody took the herb from her bag, and without even looking back, she left with their leader, or as she now discovered, the first heir of the Malric noble family.
Tears fell from her eyes as she knelt on the ground and waited for her life to end due to the betrayal from the one she loved and cared for.
In her heart, she vowed that if there was life after this, she would return and get her revenge. But alas, death is a one-time thing.
Unless you have a destiny transcending that of the living or the dead, in Aria’s case, she did, and thus, fate decided to step in.
Just when she was at her last leg, a dark portal opened, and a hooded figure with green eyes riding a shadowmare stepped out and stopped before her.
"Revenge is for the night, for they shall scream as you burn them with the flames of vengeance. Your destiny doesn’t want you to die here, Aria; you are to rise and ride into the night.

Your destiny wills you to heed the call of our master and ride into battle with him. So, I call you to rise and ride with me using the night’s flames, the Night Riders’ Authority, and my name, Kael Duskbane."
Uncle Drew, now in his Night Riders form, extended his hand, and Aria took it without hesitation.

Soon, her horse also rose from the ground and transformed into a shadowmare, and she mounted it, and like what happened to Uncle Drew, she also transformed into a hooded figure. But there was something different about her.
It was like she hadn’t fully taken her Night Rider form yet.
"Let’s go and greet our master, for it is said the Riders of the Night shall grace the battlefields once more."

chapters.title: Chapter 135: Harem Tower
paragraphs: "Huh, I feel like I suddenly became stronger," Kent said, flexing his arm to see if his strength had risen. He had just arrived at the Harem Tower to check the unlocked features and how they looked.
[True. The master has indeed received a 20% boost from the Legion Tower. It seems to come from the Riders of the Night.]
"Does that mean Uncle Drew has found another rider?" Kent asked, but he immediately knew the answer.
Per the benefits he would receive whenever a new member is added to the Riders of the Night, he would get a 20% boost in all his stats. So, it meant Uncle Drew had indeed found a new rider.
[But this is temporary. It seems you first have to invoke the new member’s True Name in order to unlock their full power and officially make them a Night Rider. Until then, this is a temporary boost]
"I see. I will look forward to that day then," Kent smiled.
[No need to look too far; you can use the Legion Call ability to summon them. But don’t worry, they can also come to you when ready.]
Kent nodded. "Can I see my status page? I want to see the boost I received."
Name: Kent
Age: 18
Bloodline: Primordial Chaos Dragon (5%)
Class: Alchemist (Master)
SubClass: Swordsman (Pseudo Master) | Soul Cultivation (Tier 3)
Cultivation: Root Grandmaster - Lvl 1/9
Physical Strength: 655 (+131)
Physical Agility: 655 (+131)
Physical Stamina: 695 (+139)
Spiritual Strength: 1,045 (+209)
Mental Strength: 835 (+167)
[Tower Points: 999,000]
[Attribute Points: 360]
[Skill Upgrade Points: 21,100]

paragraphs: After leaving the Harem Tower, Kent went to the Servant Tower. However, unlike the other towers, this one had nothing unique. It was just a plain space where he could have built a city for his servants if he wanted to.

He didn’t have the funds to build a city just yet, so he left a few minutes later and visited the Legion Tower. But, just like the Servant Tower, that place also required him to build a city or barracks for his legion.
Leaving there, he went to the Soul Tower.
"This place is really made for soul cultivation. Just breathing seems to affect my cultivation," Kent said, taking a long, deep breath that filled his mood with joy.

[This place boosts the master’s absorption speed by 60% and comprehension speed by 80%. So you don’t have to worry too much about your soul cultivation. After all, the more people you add to the tower, the stronger you get.
The only thing you need to focus on is Alchemy and Swordsmanship. But, of course, you would have to learn your soul techniques manually to ensure you have a good grasp of them.]
"I won’t say I’m not impressed—that’s because I am impressed, Gaia. Well done. After this, I’ll donate some tower points to a good cause."
After observing the tower for a while, Kent moved toward the Pagoda that stood on a small mountain.
[That is a technique given to you by Goddess Vexthra. You can access it now and learn by passing some trials, but its true nature will open when you become a Root Sage.
It was the restriction Goddess Vexthra placed on it. But if you want, I can break the restriction so you can access the true technique directly.]
"No. Let’s follow her timeline. She knew the reason why she made it so, so let’s respect that," Kent stopped her.
Vexthra is his woman, and if she restricted something meant to aid him, he would have to respect that and only access it when he is ready, and the restriction is lifted.
"Let’s go to the Guardian Tower. I will return here soon. I need to take my soul cultivation to at least Tier 5 before the Pill Master competition in three months."
A second later, they arrived in a room where the only thing inside was a giant screen showing three words: ’Gaia’s Guardian Shop.’
"What is this place, Gaia?" Kent asked, looking strangely at the screen.

[This is the guardian Tower master. This tower is all about protecting your wards, and since Tower City is where those you want can stay, this place is where you shop for the various ways to see that your wards are protected.
I have hundreds of ways, but since this is just the initial awakening of the tower, I will present only two items you can purchase right now]
Kent didn’t immediately say anything. He waited for Gaia to show what she had for him. Honestly, he wasn’t planning on building a City at each tower.
Instead of building cities, he can build training spaces for them. During his time at the Tower shop, he saw something called [Dungeon Master Card]
If he buys one and uses it, it will teleport him to an unconquered dungeon where he can use the card to claim it and move it into the tower if he manages to conquer it.
In fact, it wasn’t just dungeons; even trial grounds and ruins could be claimed for him. Basically, if he wants, he can steal anything into his tower.
So he wasn’t disappointed when he discovered this place was unlike the others.
[For now, these are the other two things I have inside the Guardian Tower]
An image of a spiderlike creature appeared. It has six eyes and six sharp legs. Kent didn’t even need to use appraisal skills to grab its details. It was already on it.
[Name: Six Eyes Shadow Spider]
[Grade: Tier 7 (Root Sage)]
-- The Six Eyes Shadow Spider is a spider beast that, when in the shadows, can remain undetected by even those three realms above it.
-- It also has 6 eyes that can look all around and far into the distance.
-- It’s incredibly fast and can be escaped easily.
-- Because of their sneaky nature, they are perfect for spying on others without them ever noticing their presence in their shadows.
<Skills>
<Poison Silk>
-- It shoots poison threads from its mouth that, when latched on the target, will poison them easily. Poison is effective against even those two realms above it.
<Enhanced Sight>
-- the Six Eyes Shadow Spider can see many miles ahead because of its many eyes.
<Enhance Hearing>
-- The Six Eyes Shadow Spider has incredible hearing. It can be heard up to 10 miles away.
<Extract>
-- The Six Eyes Shadow Spider can extract the memory of any victim they personally kill.
[Upgradable using Beast Cores]
[Price: 800,000 Tower Points]
"Not a bad item you have there, Gaia. But why is it so expensive? It’s not like it has the means to actively battle, despite being a Root Sage."
[The master forgets that you have to get close to someone to place a tracker on them. But even if I place a tracker on them, I couldn’t kill them remotely.
Also, there is a chance my tracker won’t work when they enter certain secret domains.
However, with this beast, you can monitor and kill them anytime. In fact, if you have this, your first quest can be cleared while you are hundreds of miles away.
Also, if you buy one, I will throw in another for free.]
"Fine, but let me see the other item. I will buy this, but only when it’s nearing the auction."
[Great,] Gaia beams with joy after securing a deal. She then shows the next item.
The next item appears, and it is a humanoid figure made purely of metal. It has metal armor and two long swords strapped to its back. Its red eyes glow faintly, with red strips lining its body.
[Name: Dual-Wielding Obsidian Doll]
[Grade: Great Sage (Peak)]
[Class: Dual wielder]
-- A doll created from obsidian dark metal known for its durability. It is made purely for combat. It’s mostly known as the Sentinel Guardian because it’s made to protect.
-- It has enhanced close combat abilities that don’t pale compared to a Saint Swordsman.
-- It can learn techniques related to the sword. It can also wield other weapons if you provide it (They must be dual weapons).
-- It uses the Fire, Ice, and Lightning elements.
-- It has a fast recovery rate, so it only needs to recuperate for a few hours to recover when damaged in battle.
-- It has no feelings and can only listen and obey the instructions of its master.
-- Its weapons are indestructible.
[Upgradable using Rare Metals]
[Price: 5,000,000 Tower points]
"Gaia, I will be using the One-Time Purchase Pass to buy this doll... please," Kent smiled as he said that. He wanted the expert in close combat the moment he saw it.
Why? Because he needed an expert in close combat instead of dummies to train with. But more importantly, he needed a trump card—someone or something he could rely on to save his ass when in trouble.
With this doll, he felt secure from now on. And with him about to expose his secret as the Perfect Alchemist soon, he needed all the protection he could get.
[Purchase complete. Item has been shipped to the tower storage.]
Kent immediately used his connection and summoned the doll, which appeared to be standing 3 meters tall.

"This is perfect. With this, I can gallivant anywhere without a care for danger." His laughter beamed as he examined the doll for a while. After being satisfied, he left the tower to care for things on the outside.

"A heavenly being, a dark being, and the bearer of good karma. How is this possible?" she muttered before forming a hand seal.
The white and dark stars vanished, leaving only the multicolored one. She gazed intently at the star for a few minutes before taking a crystal from her space ring.

paragraphs: "Kent, repeat what you just heard. I think I heard you wrong," Vexthra, who was reading a novel in the god realm, dropped her tablet, her eyes widening in disbelief.
One might say a goddess should have seen and heard it all so nothing could surprise or shock them. But from the look on her face, one could tell she was utterly stunned.
[Your new sister, my fourth wife, is an Aetherwarden—specifically, an Astra Sentinel,] Kent repeated. After reading about Elsa having three soul sentinels, he contacted Vexthra.
The reaction he received was far more exaggerated than expected. The goddess of hate and resentment had now begun flipping through a book with her mind.
A few seconds later, an image appeared of a female warrior with twelve pairs of wings on her back, holding a longsword and a disc-shaped artefact.
Behind her stood thousands of sentinels of various shapes and forms: knights, archers, mages, paladins, warlocks, and many more.
Vexthra skimmed through the pages until she arrived at one with the title and name "The Universal Soul Army - Astra Sentinel Legion."
Her body shuddered as she read the words.
The page detailed the rise and fall of the Astra Sentinel, the last known Aetherwarden, who died during the Chaos Era.

From the passage, it was said that she led her army into battle along with her allies, who heralded the Battle of Evolution during that era. It was a chaotic confrontation where many prominent heroes fell.
It was there that she perished alongside her army of Soul Sentinels, said to be one of the most destructive forces ever to grace the face of the universe.
It wasn’t an exaggeration for the pages of history books to call her the Princess of Battle or the Harbinger of Souls.
Vexthra skimmed through thousands of pages within seconds, a stark contrast to her leisurely pace when reading web novels.

"Kent, please tell me you have indeed added her to the harem. Although I can feel her connection, I want a verbal or telepathic confirmation," Vexthra asked, looking quite happy for someone filled with hate and resentment.

[Don’t worry, she is now smitten with me. She wouldn’t be going anywhere,] Kent smiled. Elsa was busy giving him a blowjob, oblivious to the fact that a meeting between a mortal and a goddess was taking place about her.

"Good. Now listen to me, and listen well. I don’t know the kind of True Names your tower is bestowing on my sisters and those linked to the tower, but I know that an Aetherwarden—or specifically an Astra Sentinel—is not an ordinary person.

The history books portray her as someone with extraordinary karma, someone who accomplished legendary feats in her past life. Let me tell you, if she is the same Astra Sentinel, then know she is someone who will help you greatly.

In fact, you should understand more about the nature of the True Names you are giving your people. First, it was the Riders of the Night, and now an Astra Sentinel. Just what kind of person are you, Kent?"
"What can I say? I am the son of the universe. All the good things must stay in the family," Kent smiled.
Vexthra rolled her eyes, but she couldn’t deny it. She had already seen enough to know that perhaps the resentful soul she had taken an interest in was no ordinary mortal.
For now, she wouldn’t make any assumptions, but in her mind, there was only one title to describe Kent, and it was a title gods would kill for.
’Karma Chosen.’
A Karma Chosen is, essentially, someone whom Karma wouldn’t affect. In fact, if he were to kill someone who shouldn’t be killed, Karma would still not touch him. He was immune to it.
This also meant that all good things would eventually get to him, no matter how hard other forces tried to block it.
"I want to talk to her," Vexthra said, her mood brightening.
[I’m afraid she can’t talk now. Her mouth is busy at the moment.] Kent grinned as he said that.

Vexthra, understanding his meaning, smiled but didn’t respond. She licked her lips and decided to continue her conversation with Kent for another five minutes. Then, Kent asked a question that took her aback.
[Vexthra dear, do you have a True Name?]

"I do, but it’s not something fancy. In fact, I think the True Names you have are not the ordinary kind," Vexthra replied with a weak smile. Indeed, her True Name was nothing special. She had received it when she became a goddess.
It didn’t give her any buffs or change her meaningfully.
Kent didn’t answer immediately. Instead, he first conversed with Gaia, who pointed out something that widened Kent’s smile several folds.
’If I am not mistaken, these True Name contains the inheritance of the ones it once belonged to.’ That was what Gaia had said.
In other words, one day, Elsa would become the Astral Sentinel of this generation, and if she didn’t die, she would rise above the previous wielder of the name.
[For now, all benefits for you are locked, but once I ascend to a higher world, they will be unlocked. When that happens, I will bestow upon you a True Name,] Kent declared with absolute conviction.
Vexthra nodded as small tears fell from her eyes. She was a goddess, and as she said, her True Name was simply a mark of her divinity.
But now, if she were to receive something like Elsa’s, she would become several times more powerful.
After their connection ended, Vexthra returned to her books and began researching more about the Astral Sentinel.
Now that she understood Elsa’s potential, she was determined to ensure Elsa would grow several times stronger.
Why?
Because an Astral Sentinel is someone with the potential to boost his man’s army, she may be a goddess, but she wouldn’t be able to help his man in battle.
So, she will help her sisters do that for her while she aids them using her divinity. One might call it the perfect harem.
Kent looked at Elsa, who was licking her lips with a blissful smile on her face.
"How strong are you in your mortal form? I know you are a Saint, but I don’t think you are an ordinary Saint," Kent asked.
Elsa smiled and raised five fingers.
"For now, I am a Level 6 Saint, but my strength is at least five times that. With my current power, let’s just say I wouldn’t suffer taking on a Sage or two."
"I just need to increase my mastery of my sword. I used to use a spear, but that isn’t an option anymore. I need to refine my sword skills," Elsa said, making Kent smile.

"You don’t have to worry. My master will help you get into the Divine Palace Sect. After all, you’re currently 22 years old—I’d say that’s a cheat," Kent said before pouncing on her, and for the rest of the night, they never stopped having sex.
When daybreak came, they left to see the other ladies, who were patiently waiting for them while Li Hua baked banana cakes for everyone.

chapters.title: Chapter 144: Mom, Is That Really You
paragraphs: Three damsels and Li Hua stood wide-eyed, gazing at the otherworldly beauty beside Kent. They couldn’t believe their eyes.
However, the fact that they were standing upright showed they weren’t entirely lost in their shock. They were, without a shred of doubt, stunned.
Kent and Elsa had just arrived at the other mansion, where Saintess Selene, Unity, Lilian, and Li Hua were spending the morning tasting various flavours of banana cakes she had baked.
When Kent told them the otherworldly beauty was the former Cynthia, they were all stunned—Li Hua merely imitated their expressions.
But their shock was unmistakable.
"Mom, is that really you?" Lilian asked, trying to confirm.
Elsa laughed at Lilian’s question. "I think it would be best if you just refer to me as Elsa. But to answer your question—yes, I am still your mother, though I am also a new version of myself."
Her explanation was clear. Kent just smiled, knowing although she had a new body, her milk was still there for him to have his fill whenever he wanted.
It seemed the universe was on his side.
"What happened?" Saintess Selene asked. She appeared composed on the surface, but inwardly, she was very shocked—and jealous.
They all were.
Looking at the silver-haired beauty beside Kent, who not only regained her maidenhood with a new body but also became stronger and more beautiful and de-aged, filled them with envy.
"One thing led to another, and Cynthia became Elsa. Cool, right?" Kent laughed as he said that.
He didn’t know how to explain everything to them, but he also didn’t want to make it seem like he could easily do what he did to Elsa to them.

It was a process, and his hands were tied without the token and a suitable true name. Of course, the tower had told him all his women would receive a true name. But as to how it would happen would depend on when.
"I see. Then can you make us look more beautiful too?" Unity asked.
Kent just smiled and shook his head. "For now, I can’t promise, but don’t worry, I will soon make you ladies not only beautiful but also very strong."
Kent knew he didn’t have to give false hope, but he also wouldn’t tell them he couldn’t do it. Of course, he could do it; it would just take a couple of months at most.
But he was sure they would forget about this for now once he took them to the tower.
As for whether he should take his master, too, despite her not being part of the harem yet, that would depend on whether he trusted her enough.
Kent didn’t want to answer any more questions, so he let the ladies talk while he took Li Hua to see what she had cooked up while he was away on business—literally.

Kent knew that when night came, Unity and Lilian would request he transform them, too, but he didn’t have the means yet. So, he left them to talk with Elsa. Saintess Selene even joined in on the talk.
After eating all the banana cake to replenish his energy, he took Li Hua outside to catch a cool breeze, allowing Gaia to scan her body and determine what cure she needed.
In the end, he had to plant a tracker in her and use it to determine once it surfaced. He couldn’t get any information on her, but with the tracker, he was sure things would be figured out soon.
He then returned with Li Hua, and after spending some more time with the ladies, he left to explore the remaining areas of the tower.
It would be a few hours until nightfall, meaning he has days to check everything and even scan the entire store, memorizing the details of everything on sale.
Meanwhile, around 5 pm the same day, a few miles away from the Alderford Mansion, 12 figures—3 Root Great Sages and 9 Root Sages—each wearing dark clothes and a mask, could be seen camped out.
They looked suspicious, which meant they were about to do something suspicious.
They all wore masks, but from how they were looking toward the Alderford mansion, it seemed that was their destination.
These figures were the men sent by the Dark Devil Church to kill everyone at the Alderford Mansion. Their mission was to eliminate them all.
"When night falls, we will use the cover of darkness to hunt them like we do and make sure no trace leads back to us," one of the Root Great Sages said, making the 9 Root Sages nod in agreement.
They were professionals, so they knew when to act and when to retreat. This had to be a successful mission, or their butts would be on the line.
"We move out at ten. The three of us will make sure the saintess is handled, so don’t make any mistakes on your end."
The nine figures nodded and started preparing ahead of time. With a team like theirs, things should work out well—right?
"Gaia, I think you’re trying to scam me. How can a simple sex magazine cost 10,000 tower points?" Kent said, looking at the screen of a magazine that contained sex-related content.

Unity had used the connection between them to tell her about the struggles of his master, and he wanted to help her. He had read loads of these magazines back on Earth, so he knew they would be perfect for her.
The problem, however, was the price tag Gaia had plastered on it.
[I think the master is forgetting something. Acquiring these magazines involves travelling across dimensions. 10k tower points is even cheap.]
Kent scoffed, knowing the unruly tower was just being a hard ass.
"How about this: you give me this for free, and I’ll allow you to develop the new tower prison design.
I won’t argue with whatever design you come up with," Kent offered, knowing the tower wasn’t the usual system and didn’t compromise.
[Deal. But throw in a perk. How about you let me play with the little human? I mean, you’ll need a babysitter while you get freaky with your women.]
"Deal," Kent smiled.
The magazine was transferred to his tower storage. Also, his pain of carrying the little human around had now been resolved.
If only he realized Gaia only offered because she found an interest in how Li Hua always managed to extort money from Kent.

In a few days’ time, he would find out the prices of things in the store would be changed again, and this time, the bargaining would be done by none other than the future lethal assassins who would shake the hearts of immortals.
Kent went on for days inside the tower until the clock struck 9 pm outside. He was planning to leave, but then Gaia gave him news that made him smile slightly.
Gaia had just informed him that he would soon have visitors who like to walk at night.
Of course, Kent expected something like that, so he had made Gaia monitor miles around the mansion. Now, he had new fish to fry.
Kent didn’t immediately leave; instead, he began planning how to handle the visitors, who had no idea they had been discovered.

sentences.text: Three damsels and Li Hua stood wide-eyed, gazing at the otherworldly beauty beside Kent.
They couldn’t believe their eyes.
However, the fact that they were standing upright showed they weren’t entirely lost in their shock.
They were, without a shred of doubt, stunned.
Kent and Elsa had just arrived at the other mansion, where Saintess Selene, Unity, Lilian, and Li Hua were spending the morning tasting various flavours of banana cakes she had baked.
When Kent told them the otherworldly beauty was the former Cynthia, they were all stunned—Li Hua merely imitated their expressions.
But their shock was unmistakable.
"Mom, is that really you?" Lilian asked, trying to confirm.
Elsa laughed at Lilian’s question.
"I think it would be best if you just refer to me as Elsa.

Her explanation was clear.

It seemed the universe was on his side.

She appeared composed on the surface, but inwardly, she was very shocked—and jealous.
They all were.
Looking at the silver-haired beauty beside Kent, who not only regained her maidenhood with a new body but also became stronger and more beautiful and de-aged, filled them with envy.
"One thing led to another, and Cynthia became Elsa.
Cool, right?" Kent laughed as he said that.

Of course, the tower had told him all his women would receive a true name.

chapters.title: Chapter 145: Formation Stones, Planning an Ambush
paragraphs: The clock would soon hit ten, so the assassins chose to close in on the mansion, thinking that with their superior concealing abilities, they could stay hidden from the sensing range of anyone below the Root Great Sage stage.
Saintess Selene was just a Root Sage, so they weren’t worried.
But Gaia picked up on them when they entered the range Kent had told her to cover. It was 6 miles from the mansion.
There was no escaping her, even if you were a god.
But now that they were discovered, Kent could only prepare.
"How many are we talking, Gaia?" Kent asked.
[Three Great Sages and 9 Root Sages.]
"I see. This is cool then. Even though I can’t handle a Root Great Sage, I have somebody who can do that. The only question here is whether we can kill them all before they escape."
He wasn’t worried about whether or not he could face them. He knew he could do that now that his Soul Master class had become a Grandmaster, too.
[With just 10,000 tower points, you can buy Formation Stones to create a formation around the battleground, preventing any of them from escaping.
With 15,000 points, you can even block sounds, and with 20,000, you can prevent lights from attacks from being noticed.]
Gaia offered, making Kent nod in understanding.

"Let’s go with the 20,000. I will be getting the points back anyway," Kent said with a calm smile. He wasn’t about to pretend he would be able to kill all of them before they had the chance to escape.
So he needed help, and with this formation, he could do just what he had in mind. With the formation, he could fight to his heart’s content.
"But Gaia, how am I going to set the formations without them noticing me first?" Kent asked.
[I will handle your aura. Just do your thing, and I will handle the rest.]
The tower can conceal his aura, making it impossible to notice his presence unless you look directly at him. That was the perk of having a tower.
Kent spent the 20,000 points and bought the formation stones.
When activated, these stones contained formations that would cover an entire area where the stones had been meticulously arranged. Only he could come and go as he pleased.
After leaving the tower, he used his [blink] skill to move and create an 8km diameter box as the kill zone for the visitors he and the battle doll would be handling.
He still had about 40 minutes before the assassins made their move. But with the formation active, he left and returned to the mansion.
He would be spending the night with Lilian and Unity, but before that, he called his master and handed her the magazine.
"No need to be shy, master. This is just something to prepare you for the journey ahead," Kent said, licking his lips.
Saintess Selene blushed.
She couldn’t directly ask Unity or Lilian what she wanted to know, but now that she has a magazine, she could learn something.
In fact, in her heart, she was overjoyed.
With her perception level, she could tell Elsa had become stronger than her. She wasn’t the same just a day ago.
This got her thinking, and as a very curious person, she couldn’t help but wonder what had happened to her. She was already looking forward to her awakening ceremony without even realising it.
Kent walked up to her and held her by the waist.
"You don’t have to rush things. We’ll be going back to the academy in a week’s time, so if you want to wait until then, I don’t mind at all."
He kissed her for a second and then pulled back, but he still held her by the waist.
It took her a few seconds, but she kissed him back, and within minutes, they were locked in, kissing. After they broke the kiss, Kent told her to relax and enjoy her reading.
He left and stepped outside the mansion, ensuring he stayed only 100 meters away from the formation and concealed so he wouldn’t be noticed. The tower also made sure his aura wasn’t leaking.
He wanted to see them first and plan his attack.
A few minutes before ten, twelve people could be seen sneaking closer to the mansion. Kent smiled and waited.
Just when they got within 100 meters of him, they stopped. It seemed they had come to a dead end. Something was blocking their way.
"What is it?" one of the Root Great Sages asked.

"Leader, it seems there is a formation blocking us," one of the Root Sages replied. The leader came closer and inspected it using his energy, and as the Sage said, indeed, there was a formation in their way.
"This wasn’t here the last time," one of the three leaders said.
With the masks on their faces, it was impossible to tell their expressions, but Kent knew they must be freaking out by now.
Of course, he wasn’t concerned about that. He just watched them try attacking the formation, but nothing worked. They used other means, but they all resulted in the same failure.
So, they chose to combine their strength to attack. But that didn’t happen, as before they could do that, Kent appeared 40 meters from them.
"Are you guys from the Dark Devil Church or the Hand?" Kent asked, feigning ignorance. He already knows the answer, having gotten it using his enchanted eyes.
But he just had to ask.
"Who are you?" one of the leaders asked.
Kent scoffed. "I should be the one asking that. You guys are trespassing, and as such, I should be the one asking what the hell you’re doing here.
But I know you’re here to kill everyone, just like you did with the Ashlands." Kent’s words shook the hearts of the three leaders.
That mission was supposed to be a secret, yet it was made known by a random, weak youth.
"I presume you’re here for the Atomic Divine Body... right?" Kent asked again.
"Y-You, who are you?"
"So it’s true. Then that means I have the right bunch. Don’t worry, I just need the location of your headquarters. But don’t worry, I won’t torture you for it; your dead bodies can answer me."
Kent moved closer. "And before you act tough, know that the entire space has been sealed. So, no matter what you try, you won’t be able to escape.
Your death has already been signed."
Kent summoned the Battle Doll, who immediately appeared and stood tall beside him. It quickly drew the two swords behind it.
"Take care of those three," Kent said, pointing at the three Root Great Sages.
The doll moved, and before the three Root Great Sages could react, it appeared and unleashed a powerful attack that immediately separated them from the nine Root Sages.
Kent looked at them. "It is true I can’t handle you nine at the same time, but that doesn’t mean I can’t handle you."
"Soul Shock!" Kent unleashed the skill he bought from the Green Gate Bazaar last time. Immediately, the nine held their heads, a few screaming.
A black pill appeared in his hand. It was a poison pill he concocted the last time. It was called the Dark Menace Poison Pill.
Also, it was a bomb-type pill, and right now, Kent threw it at the nine, which exploded in their faces immediately, making all of them scream.
His sword appeared, and he smiled.

chapters.title: Chapter 146: The Terrifying Battle Doll
paragraphs: (A/N: For the sake of creating a good fight scene, I will call the three Root Great Sages Leader 1, 2, and 3. No need to name assassins since they choose to remain incognito)
BOOM
Leader 2 was thrown meters away by a powerful kick from the battle doll. The force of the kick was evident as he landed face-first on the ground.
Kent turned to look at the battered and bruised Root Great Sage. A portion of his mask had been ripped off from the fall, with cracks spreading across its surface.
The other two charged at the doll, but it effortlessly parried their dagger attacks, making them wince as none of their strikes landed.
The battle had started two minutes ago, yet the three leaders were utterly powerless. They don’t appear much in front of the Peak Great Sage battle Doll.
On the other hand, the doll was dismantling them with ease. It wasn’t using any active techniques, just a good old-fashioned sword fight.
Kent observed with surprise how efficiently it fought. For someone aspiring to walk the sword’s path, Kent saw a promising training partner in the doll.
While the doll mercilessly toyed with the three leaders, the Sages fared no better.
Perhaps, if Kent had been solely a sword cultivator, they might have stood a chance. Unfortunately for them, he was also a soul cultivator with over 50,000 soul essences to fuel his soul attacks.
But that wasn’t all. Kent was also an Alchemist who had developed a peculiar interest in crafting poison pills while studying recipes for Tier 2 pills.
Thus, he created some particularly nasty pills—16 out of the 30 Tier 2 pills he had concocted.
With his mastery of over 7,000 sword plays, formidable soul cultivation, and expertise in alchemy, Kent was practically toying with the Sages.
5 of the 9 Sages were already poisoned and near their death doors. Their poisons are different, so the effect is different and nasty.
One was literally ripping the flesh off his face. The poison was a nasty one that made one skin burn so hot and get itchy that their base instincts would be to claw their skin.
Kent’s only move was to parry their attacks, and then, using the dagger Manager Alina sent him, he would take their masks off, and then, with a kick to the jaw, the month would open.
The pill follows through after that.
It was a combined precise series of attacks, but Kent pulled it off effortlessly. The feeling was so natural to him.
[Rapid Slash]
Ten arcs of sword qi flash out from his sword.

The healthy four arching deep within their soul felt doom in the form of sword arcs moving toward them. The attack landed on them, forcing three to be pushed back because they couldn’t defend fast enough.
Thus, the last one standing was the first kill.
Kent used [Blink] and appeared behind him. The next second, his head was on the ground.
[You have killed a Root Sage.]
[You have received +500 Soul Essense and Successfully extracted their memory]
[You have received +10,000 Tower points & +100 Skill Upgrade Points]
[You have received a Soul-Spirit.]
Kent grinned and moved toward the three who had managed to resist his attempts to poison them. But their resistance was futile—they would die for sure.
The other five were in even worse shape, and though Kent knew they would succumb sooner or later, he wasn’t one to let them linger in suffering.
Without hesitation, he moved swiftly, dispatching them efficiently before returning to the three sages who had started to flee.
"Running is futile, brothers. It would be better to face your deaths like true men," Kent called out, sprinting after them.
"What did we ever do to you? We’re just workers fulfilling a contract!" one of them shouted, his voice trembling, just as Kent caught up and drove his sword through the man’s neck.
The blade was so sharp that the sage likely didn’t even feel the fatal strike.
Well, Kent mused, perhaps the 10,002 sword techniques he was practising were essential after all. His swordsmanship had advanced to a level where even hand-to-hand close combat posed no challenge.
"Take solace in your death, knowing that soon, your employers will follow you," Kent stopped and watched as the two sages ran around the formation like children.
Meanwhile, the battle doll had severed the head of Leader Three. It was a clean cut with no smudges, showing just how lethal the doll was.
Leader Two was looking rather pathetic.
His left leg was cut off, and, well, his left arm was also severed.
’That looks painful.’
The right arm was also gone, and he was bleeding all over. Strangely, he was still moving with a single leg, clinging to the belief that he might still be able to kill the unkillable doll.
’Maybe his brain was also cut somewhere.’
Kent turned to Leader One, who was now lying on the floor with a thousand cuts on his body. Blood oozed from him, making him appear rather pitiful to the eye, but he wasn’t having any fun either.
’Gaia, I will need a comprehensive list of the best sword combat techniques you have. It will be great to create a monster out of this bastard.’
Kent was thrilled.
Well, the scene was horrible, but the surgical precision the doll was carrying out the slaughter thrilled him. His blood was boiling.
’Something is definitely wrong with me’
Kent charged at the sages, who seemed to have hit a wall—literally.
The next few seconds were spent dispatching the two sages, who appeared to have given up. Well, the situation hadn’t been in their favour to begin with.

Kent was simply too monstrous. With his relentless soul attacks, the sages couldn’t focus, leaving him with plenty of openings to exploit. In their current state, they were powerless to do much of anything.
Perhaps, if they had been Root Great Sages, the battle would have been much easier. But there are no regrets in a fight to the death.
They came to kill, but instead, they are being killed. One could find the irony in that.
Twenty-five minutes later, the battle ended with all twelve assassins slain. Gaia consumed their memories and began piecing them together to uncover a way for Kent to get to the root of the problem.
The doll sheathed its swords and stood innocently as though it hadn’t just finished torturing three Root Great Sages.
"Good job, buddy. We’ll have you crossing over to the Root Transcendent stage soon enough." Kent’s laughter rang out before he dismissed the doll.
He asked Gaia to scan their bodies for something valuable. Ultimately, he found a dark token and a good mask that he would use soon enough.

After that, he gathered the bodies and burned them. After making sure everything was settled, Kent took down the formation and then left to have some fun with his lovers, who were eagerly waiting for him.
But of course, he had things to do, and one of them was to get back to manage Alina. He also needed to check the gifts Vexthra had given him when he visited the god realm.
She called them trinkets, but he knew better. Anything from a god is not a trinket. Perhaps, to them, it might seem that way, but to mortals, it’s a treasure worth killing for.
